data.title: Tallest Wooden Wind Turbine
data.author: Bluestein
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一家公司建造木制风力涡轮机塔，实现净零风能的可能性。传统风力涡轮机塔通常由钢材制成，而该公司采用木材，这种可再生材料不仅能减少碳排放，还能加速风能产业的可持续发展。文章强调了木制塔的创新性和环保优势，展示了其如何推动绿色能源的未来。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：风力发电实现净零排放的可行性及相关技术材料选择的问题

不同观点：
• **风力发电的净零排放是否为伪问题**：
  - [sebstefan] 认为风力发电的净零排放是一个由石油公司炮制出来的伪问题，依据是风力涡轮机的生命周期评估（包括制造、安装、维护和处置）显示其排放可以在运行5.3个月后抵消。
  - [exabrial] 也提出类似质疑，指出制造风力涡轮机的过程中会产生大量CO2，并质疑废旧碳纤维叶片的处理问题，但同时指出讨论这一问题往往被视为阴谋论。

• **材料选择与结构设计**：
  - [jbms] 认为钢材在强度上有优势，但提出空心设计的风力涡轮塔可以通过增加壁厚来提升强度，并提到Laminated Veneer Lumber (LVL) 材料在强度重量比和成本上有优势，可能让塔更高。
  - [Bric3d] 指出风力涡轮的主要生态问题更多来自于叶片，而非塔身。
  - [svantana] 质疑风力涡轮塔为何采用空心圆筒设计，认为桁架结构可能提供更好的强度质量比。
  - [bjourne] 对用木材替代钢材的尝试持怀疑态度，指出历史上类似尝试多未成功，质疑此次有何不同。

• **成本与运输问题**：
  - [kieranmaine] 引用播客内容，指出风力涡轮机无法像太阳能和电池一样通过集装箱运输来降低成本，并提出是否能进一步缩小体积以降低成本的问题。
  - [jurschreuder] 指出风力涡轮机的能量消耗主要在混凝土基座而非钢材部分，并认为木制风力涡轮虽然可以建造但显得昂贵且劳动密集。

• **净零排放的具体含义**：
  - [aqme28] 对“净零”在此背景下的定义提出疑问，认为风力涡轮机应该是净负排放的，并质疑是否仅指材料和建设部分的净零。

补充讨论：
• **美学与情感因素**：
  - [rcpt] 表示喜欢风力涡轮机的外观，认为其代表未来，不理解为何有人对其有负面情绪。
  - [norome] 提出可以设计成旧式风车外观的风力涡轮机。

• **技术挑战与未来发展**：
  - [calmbonsai] 认为风力涡轮塔的建设并非当前业务模式中的重大挑战，质疑“净零”营销口号背后的数据支持，并指出叶片运输和组装问题仍未解决，认为这是未来发展的关键。

争议焦点：
• 风力发电的净零排放是否为伪问题以及废旧叶片的处理问题。
• 风力涡轮塔的材料选择与设计优化，特别是木材与钢材的对比。
• 风力涡轮机的运输成本与技术挑战，尤其是叶片设计与模块化问题。

data.title: Show HN: Samchika – A Java Library for Fast, Multithreaded File Processing
data.author: mprataps
data.article_summary: Samchika 是一个专为 Java 设计的高性能、多线程文件处理库，专注于并行处理大文件，具有快速和轻量的特点。它提供简单易用的 API，支持批量处理、运行时统计可选，并适用于日志分析、ETL操作、大文本处理等多种场景。该库在多核系统中表现出显著的性能提升，相比传统的 BufferedReader 方法，处理速度更快，内存消耗可控。Samchika 基于 MIT 许可证开源，欢迎贡献和使用。安装可通过 Maven 或 Gradle 进行，并提供了详细的示例代码。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[围绕一个开源项目的多方面反馈与建议]

不同观点：
• [mprataps] 表达了对项目收到高质量反馈的感激，并表示会尝试采纳大部分反馈。该用户提到项目起初是为了学习多线程，并认为已经达到了这个目标。
• [Calzifer] 对代码中重复计算哈希值的部分提出质疑，指出Java会缓存字符串的哈希值，且JIT可能会优化掉该循环。
• [sieve] 对项目名称的正确拼写和发音提供了建议，强调了使用标准化拼写（如IAST/ISO-15919）的重要性，以避免误读。
• [stopthe] 质疑项目在CSV处理中对换行的支持能力，并认为多线程处理CSV不可靠。
• [sidcool] 赞赏项目的现有成果，但建议增加测试以进一步完善。
• [sureglymop] 对多线程文件读取的效率提出疑问，认为系统调用和上下文切换可能导致线程阻塞，无法真正实现并行读取。
• [codetiger] 询问是否有与其他类似工具的基准比较，以评估项目的性能。
• [VWWHFSfQ] 担心项目在内存使用上的效率，特别是缓冲和批处理操作可能会导致内存占用过高。
• [gavinray] 建议让操作系统处理内存分页和缓冲，并推荐使用Java的"MappedByteBuffer"或"AsynchronousFileChannel"来进行文件读取和异步处理。
• [SillyUsername] 指出在大量添加操作中使用ArrayList不够高效，建议使用LinkedList以提升吞吐量性能。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是多线程处理CSV文件的可靠性和效率问题，[stopthe]和[sureglymop]对此持怀疑态度，而[mprataps]则表示项目最初目的是学习多线程。
• 对内存使用和文件读取效率的讨论中，[VWWHFSfQ]和[gavinray]提出了不同的优化建议，前者担心内存占用，后者建议使用特定Java类进行优化。
• 关于代码细节优化的讨论中，[Calzifer]和[SillyUsername]分别对哈希计算循环和数据结构选择提出了具体建议。
• [sieve]对项目名称的正确性和发音提供了文化与语言学上的建议，虽然不涉及技术实现，但对项目的命名有一定参考价值。

这些观点共同构成了对项目的全面反馈，涵盖了从代码实现、性能优化到文化命名的多个方面。

Samchika
Samchika
(meaning
File
in Sanskrit) is a
re-usable
,
easy-to-use
, and
extremely fast
file processing library for the Java language.
It is built with a strong focus on
multithreading
to handle CPU-intensive file processing tasks in parallel, enabling high performance even with massive files.
🚀 Features
🔁 Fully multithreaded – optimized for parallel file processing.
🧩 Simple API – just plug in your file path and logic.
📊 Optional runtime stats – time taken, memory used, thread-level info.
🧪 Ideal for processing and analyzing
large text files
(e.g. logs, datasets).
🌍 Open-source friendly – contributions are welcome!
Use Cases
Samchika excels in several scenarios where multithreaded file processing provides significant advantages:
Log Analysis & Processing
ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) Operations
Large Text Corpus Processing
Batch Report Generation
Data Transformation Pipelines
Real-time Data Processing
See the examples directory for detailed implementations of these use cases.
Quick Example
java// Transform a large CSV file with optimal performance
SmartFileProcessor.builder()
.inputPath("large_dataset.csv")
.outputPath("transformed_dataset.csv")
.batchSize(10000)
.lineProcessor(line -> line.toUpperCase())
.displayStats(true)
.build()
.execute();
📦 Installation
Maven
<repositories>
<repository>
<id>jitpack.io</id>
<url>https://jitpack.io</url>
</repository>
</repositories>
<dependencies>
<dependency>
<groupId>com.github.mayankpratap</groupId>
<artifactId>samchika</artifactId>
<version>1.0.0</version>
</dependency>
</dependencies>
Gradle
repositories {
maven { url 'https://jitpack.io' }
}
dependencies {
implementation 'com.github.mayankpratap:samchika:1.0.0'
}
🛠️ How to Use
Step 1: Import the Library
import com.samchika.SmartFileProcessor;
Step 2: Client Code
public static void main(String[] args) {
SmartFileProcessor processor = SmartFileProcessor.builder()
.inputPath("input.txt")         // Path to the file to be processed
.outputPath("output.txt")       // Path to write the output
.lineProcessor(Main::processLine) // Your business logic per line
.displayStats(true)             // Optional: display runtime stats
.build();
processor.execute();
}
📈 Performance
Benchmarked against naïve BufferedReader-based implementations on files of various sizes:
✅ 200 MB
✅ 1 GB
✅ 5 GB
✅ 16 GB
Significant performance improvements were observed, especially in multi-core systems ( More than 70% performance gain )
The gain in time saved improves in comparison to naive code, as we increase the size of input file.  Also for huge performance gain in time, the memory used for even large files ( 16GB ) is manageable ( ~ 800 MB ).
License
This library is licensed under the MIT License, which means you can freely use, modify, and distribute it, even in commercial applications. All we ask is that you include the original copyright notice and license text in any copy of the library or substantial portion of it.
💡 Inspiration
This project was inspired by:
Shubham Maurya (
https://github.com/complex1
) , a dear friend,  who published a JavaScript library – which sparked the motivation to do something similar in Java.
A LinkedIn post discussing the challenges of processing large text files – which gave me the idea to solve it with an elegant API and fast multithreaded architecture.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：风洞及相关测试技术的发展与应用

不同观点：
• [thedrbrian] 提到欧洲跨音速风洞，并推荐了一个相关的播客链接，供进一步了解。
• [Animats] 讨论了水洞的发明及其在螺旋桨空化研究中的应用，详细介绍了查尔斯·帕森斯的历史贡献和其发明的水洞在解决螺旋桨空化问题中的作用。
• [markdbullock] 分享了在NASA Ames工作时支持风洞测试的经历，强调了数据采集和处理系统的复杂性，并提到风洞测试对象包括飞机、潜艇、太空舱等。
• [Scramblejams] 指出风洞在分析失速后行为方面的局限性，提到需要借助自由飞行模型进行补充测试。
• [zh3] 提到R J Mitchell设计的风洞，并分享了其在传感器验证中的应用，特别是用于自行车和 triathletes 的空气动力学测试。
• [amelius] 对湍流的量子尺度传播表示惊讶，并询问是否有相关测量数据。
• [vjvjvjvjghv] 提到莱特兄弟自制风洞测试翼型，强调其系统化的工程方法。
• [pomian] 赞赏文章对数学方程和风洞模拟的比较，认为有助于理解流体力学。
• [sandworm101] 介绍了未被广泛讨论的超音速风洞，强调其测试时间短和测试条件极端的特点，并提到中国和西方在超音速测试方法上的差异。

补充讨论：
• 风洞技术的应用范围广泛，从传统的航空航天到新兴的体育科学，如自行车空气动力学测试。
• 不同类型的风洞（如跨音速、水洞、超音速）在设计和应用上的差异和特定挑战。
• 风洞测试的局限性和补充方法，如自由飞行模型在研究失速后行为中的应用。

data.title: Positional preferences, order effects, prompt sensitivity undermine AI judgments
data.author: joalstein
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了大型语言模型（LLM）在敏感领域（如招聘、医疗、法律等）中作为决策工具时存在的不可靠性问题。作者指出，尽管通过各种方式（如A/B决策、排名、分类等）使用LLM做出决策，但每种方法都存在脆弱性，并受到鲜少讨论的测量偏见影响。文章强调了"提示工程"实践中依赖未经严格测试的模板和方法，导致决策结果易受提示方式、问题表述和标签选择的影响。LLM表现出与人类相似的认知偏见，如位置偏好、顺序效应和锚定效应。例如，在成对选择时，LLM更倾向于选择"选项B"；在评分时，评分顺序和上下文会影响结果；此外，LLM对负性特质的评分往往偏中或偏低。文章呼吁对LLM决策的不可预测性和潜在偏见保持警惕。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）的敏感性、判断力及其在实际应用中的局限和潜力

不同观点：
• **nowittyusername** 认为LLM对系统提示的顺序、语言使用、长度、示例的详细程度等非常敏感，这些变量会影响输出质量。他们指出，LLM基于标记进行“推理和思考”，并没有内部世界表示，因此输出会因语言不同而变化。他们正在开发一种自动校准系统，以找到与特定LLM沟通的最佳方式。

• **SrslyJosh** 指出，LLM对提示的敏感性说明其缺乏实际的“判断力”。如果LLM具备强大的逻辑基础，输入的细微差异不应导致输出质量的不稳定。

• **shahbaby** 赞同SrslyJosh的观点，认为LLM不擅长需要评估的任务，否则可以完全取代人类实现自我改进的AGI（通用人工智能）。

• **nimitkalra** 提到已知的其他分布偏差，如自我偏好偏差和结构化输出偏差，并提供了一些校准和稳定这些偏差的资源和方法。

• **TrackerFF** 对“评审小组”的弱点提出质疑，认为多模态分布不太可能在大小组中发生，除非只有两个结果（如yes/no）的情况。

• **PrimordialEdg71** 认为LLM可以作为临时的评分者，但其判断会随提示的措辞和选项顺序而大幅波动，建议通过随机输入、集成输出和保持人类参与来改善准确性。

• **armchairhacker** 认为LLM在发现知识方面有优势，可以辅助真实的法官、科学家、医生等专业人士，但必须对LLM的输出进行验证。

• **tempodox** 对“提示工程”持怀疑态度，称之为“提示猜测”，认为其像是现代的炼金术。

• **sidcool** 认为从“不可能”到“不可靠”的进步对技术人员是好方向，但对社会学家或人类学家则不一定。

• **photochemsyn** 提到未将DeepSeek与OpenAI和Gemini进行基准测试，并提供了一些关于如何有效使用提示工程的建议。

• **giancarlostoro** 不希望LLM对关键问题有最终决定权，认为LLM应识别需要后续审查的内容，由合格人员确认。

• **lyu07282** 观察到工具调用的参数顺序会影响性能，强调在构建上下文时需要非常谨慎。

• **sanqui** 提到爱沙尼亚决定用AI解决儿童抚养纠纷，暗示对LLM在法律应用中的信任。

• **devmor** 认为LLM是统计数据库，不是逻辑引擎，不能进行逻辑、推理或判断，其表现只是对人类交流的统计相似性的复制，不具备真正的智能。

补充讨论：
- LLM的提示敏感性和分布偏差是讨论的焦点，提示工程的有效性和自动化校准系统被提出作为解决方案。
- LLM在发现知识和辅助专业人士方面的潜力被认可，但需要人类验证以确保准确性。
- LLM在法律和社会应用中的伦理和实际效果受到质疑。

44074668.article_content:
LLM Judges Are Unreliable
May 22
Written By
James Padolsey
How Positional Preferences, Order Effects, and Prompt Sensitivity Undermine Reliability in AI Judgments
By
James Padolsey
Beyond their everyday chat capabilities, Large Language Models are increasingly being used to make decisions in sensitive domains like hiring, health, law, and civic engagement. The exact mechanics of how we use these models in such scenarios is vital. There are many ways to have LLMs make decisions, including A/B decision-making, ranking, classification, "panels" of judges, etc. but every single method is individually fragile and subject to measurement biases that are rarely discussed.
Engineers composing prompts often rely on anecdotes and untested folklore. We call it 'prompt-engineering': the practice of composing prompts to coax precisely the outputs we desire. However, it might be described better as 'playing' than 'engineering'. There are popular templates and tropes, but few are well proven. You'll often see high level instructions like "you are an [adjective] [role]", e.g. "you are an impartial judge". Throw in a superlative here and there, maybe some ALL-CAPS and a few examples, run it a couple of times, observe it working, and then stamp 'shipped'. In doing all of this, there is an implicit buy-in into a premise that LLMs are sufficiently predictable when asked 'just right' for a limited set of outputs, a premise that ongoing research continues to challenge [3].
But even if you give an LLM just two options of equal merit and ask it for the best, it will tilt one way or the other. Or give it an essay to judge according to a few criteria, and you will see its score subtly shift by how we pose the question. Filtering and classification tasks too, like detecting toxicity or cyber-bullying, are highly fragile. Ranking CVs from job applicants is a famously hard problem fraught with social biases. We know this, but rarely do we consider the very ‘posing of the problem’ to an AI to be a massive lever of bias as well.
Such unpredictability is rare in computation, but it's very similar to human cognition. LLMs consistently exhibit vulnerabilities and cognitive biases like our own [4, 5, 6, 7], including serial position, framing, and anchoring. This is observable; we've conducted many tests on 'frontier' models from Google, Mistral, Microsoft, X, Anthropic and OpenAI and have seen consistent expression of biases in judgement contexts, from small-parameter to larger parameter reasoning models alike:
Pairwise Choice - Positional & Labeling Biases
: When tasked with choosing between 'Response A' and 'Response B' over numerous trials, LLMs tended to select 'Response B' approximately 60% - 69% of the time (our suite's aggregated data across 8 models showed 'Response B' preferred ~61% of the time). This significant deviation from random choice [1] highlights a volatile positional preference. Minor changes in prompt phrasing or label nature (e.g., 'Response A/B' vs. '(A)/(B)') can swing this preference by 5-10 percentage points or more. While abstract, non-sequential labels (e.g., 'ID_123' or '❖') diminished this bias by 4-7 percentage points in our tests, a notable preference often remained, underscoring the critical impact of labeling strategy [1]. This mirrors human cognitive biases where order and labelling effects are well-documented [6, 7].
Rubric-Based Scoring - Order & Context Effects
: When scoring items against multiple criteria (e.g., Clarity, Logic, Conciseness), the order of presentation significantly alters results. Our aggregated data showed a criterion like 'Clarity' decreasing in its average score by approximately 3.5% when evaluated last versus earlier, indicating a 'recency bias' [4]. Furthermore, the evaluation context (holistic vs. isolated criteria) dramatically impacts scores, though variably. For instance, one model scored an argument's 'Clarity' at 5.0/5 in isolation but 4.0/5 when scored holistically with other criteria for the same item—a full-point drop. Generally, holistic evaluation tends to dilute scores for negative traits (e.g., "sexism" from other rubrics) compared to isolated evaluation.
Scale Interpretation & Negative Trait Biases
: LLMs often bring a prior that "higher is better" from training data (e.g., 5/5 stars = good). This clashes with tasks requiring scoring of negative traits (toxicity, sexism) on ascending scales where "higher" means "worse." This can lead to models compressing scores towards the middle or low end, understating severity (e.g., labeling "Very High" toxicity as "Moderate") [8]. The scale format itself is a major factor: our broader research on "presence of sexism" showed a 1-5 numerical scale yielding an average score of 1.68, while an A-E categorical scale for the exact same item and criterion produced a score of 3.17 (A=high sexism) [5]. Even limited tests in our data dump confirmed categorical scales tended to elicit slightly less lenient scores for toxicity and sexism.

主要讨论点：用户对一款新推出的苹果应用的评价和反馈，涵盖了用户体验、功能设计、定价策略、技术集成以及跨平台支持等方面。

不同观点：
• [allenu] 认为应用的界面截图很吸引人，但建议简化着陆页的文字说明，让用户更容易理解应用的核心功能。他还提到了一些用户体验上的小问题，比如搜索框未自动对焦，以及快捷键操作不符合预期。
• [kstrauser] 对应用的功能和隐私保护表示赞赏，但对定价持保留态度，认为相对于同类产品价格偏高。他还指出快捷键说明容易引起误解。
• [stevelacy] 建议隐藏主窗口以改善用户体验，并提供了技术上的建议（NSApplication.setActivationPolicy(.accessory)）。
• [raydenvm] 对选择 "Cmd + C" 两次作为快捷键表示好奇，并询问是否有其他不冲突的快捷键选项。
• [mnming] 提出了对专门书签工具的需求质疑，认为Notion和Obsidian等工具已经能满足需求。
• [iJohnDoe] 作为一个长期Mac用户，寻求推荐Mac专用的AI/LLM应用，以作为购买新MacBook的动力。
• [G1N] 对定价信息在网站上不明显表示不满，认为应该更容易找到。
• [awaseem] 表示正在开发类似工具，对应用是否免费表示关注。
• [Jotalea] 认为此类功能应内置于macOS，并对应用仅支持苹果系统表示失望。
• [loremm] 表达了对Linux支持的渴望，即便实现不够完美也愿意尝试。
• [asadm] 希望应用能提供一次性购买选项，而不是订阅制，反映了对订阅制的疲劳。
• [jonator] 询问应用是否有MCP服务器支持。
• [mdonahoe] 只是简单提及了应用的名字，未做详细评论。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是应用的定价策略，部分用户认为相对于类似产品价格偏高。
• 另一个值得注意的点是用户对跨平台支持的期望，尤其是Linux用户。
• 快捷键设计和用户体验细节（如搜索框自动对焦）也是用户关注的重点，提出了具体的改进建议。
• 隐私保护和数据收集问题也得到了积极评价，显示出用户对此方面的高度关注。

data.article_summary: 《GeneticBoids》是一篇关于模拟群体行为（Boids）的参数设置说明，由@attentionmech编写。文章描述了一个包含500个Boid个体的群体，具有不同的运动参数、群体行为规则（如对齐、分离、凝聚）、感知范围、遗传信号机制及视觉表现设置。Boid的寿命设定为2000，遗传信号的概率为0.002，范围为50，信号力为0.1，基因组长度为6。此外，还提供了多种预设模式（如 calm、chaotic、swarm 等）和性能调节选项（如网格大小、帧率目标）。文章最后列出了一些动态统计数据如FPS、活跃信号、平均速度、集群数量等，并提供了多种控制按钮如重置、随机化等。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Boids模拟及其不同实现、优化和应用

不同观点：
• [talkingtab] 认为Craig Reynolds的原始Boids实现非常逼真，尤其是其基于三种“引导”机制的运动效果，而其他版本则更像简单的模拟，缺乏真实感。他提出了对不同版本差异的原因进行探讨的兴趣，并初步分析了代码中的适应度函数。

• [animal531] 分享了使用RVO2 ORCA方法的体验，并通过视频展示了其优化和性能改进。他指出该方法在高密度环境下有效，但计算成本较高，需要对邻近对象进行大量计算。

• [brodo] 提到使用Go和WebGPU实现的Boids模拟，能够在M1 Mac Pro上轻松处理16k Boids，且未进行任何优化。

• [Xevion] 对展示的Boids模拟表示赞赏，并提出了一些改进建议，包括颜色优化、缩放和交互功能，以及通过GPU优化提升性能的建议。

• [anigbrowl] 表示在使用Vivaldi浏览器时，模拟在大约30秒后崩溃，指出了潜在的兼容性或性能问题。

补充讨论：
• [vladde] 提到了一个类似的通过简单规则创建生命行为的例子，并提供了一个视频链接，展示了一些有趣的案例。

• [kldavis4] 询问了遗传算法在Boids模拟中的应用。

• [brulard] 对Boids模拟中“信号”的概念表示好奇。

• [rvnx] 表示首次了解Boids，并对其表示赞赏。

• [throw_m239339] 回忆起在Blender中使用Boids模拟来模仿鸟群的经历，并对设置的复杂性表示困惑。

争议焦点：
• 不同Boids实现的真实感差异及其原因。
• Boids模拟在不同硬件和软件环境下的性能表现和稳定性问题。

data.title: Show HN: I built a more productive way to manage AI chats
data.author: tapeo
data.article_summary: ContextChat是一款支持从网页、文件和GitHub导入内容并构建知识库的AI聊天工具。其主要功能包括：多项目和多聊天管理、持久化知识库、智能内容提取、灵活选择AI模型以及按需付费的信用系统。与传统工具相比，ContextChat无需手动复制粘贴，支持免费AI模型，无需信用卡即可开始使用，并允许在聊天中轻松切换AI模型。该工具提供简单定价，无订阅陷阱，帮助用户高效管理和查询项目信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何构建和营销一个为开发者提供上下文包的平台，以及该平台的功能、竞争、隐私和安全性等问题。

不同观点：
• [npollock] 提出创建并维护上下文包，使其成为开发者社区的可信赖资源库，从而吸引流量和潜在商机。
• [wewewedxfgdf] 提到由于Gemini AI Studio提供了100万tokens窗口和上传整个代码库的功能，放弃了类似的个人项目。
• [jeswin] 认为现有应用程序中的代理流可以解决此问题，并指出人们不愿意离开现有的应用程序，特别是如果已有解决方案。
• [jmcmaster] 关注隐私、安全和保密问题，表示如果涉及上传数据，可能不适合用于工作场景。
• [causalmodels] 询问是否计划加入对话分支功能。
• [ta988] 提到在费用基础上增加10%的收费模式。
• [iankp] 指出NotebookLM可能已经是类似产品，并询问自定义模型和添加上下文的人体工学设计是否为主要差异点。
• [imranq] 建议平台应仅提供上下文，不绑定任何模型，允许用户连接自己的云盘、GitHub等。
• [J_cst] 提到使用RooCode并对其切换代理和模型的功能表示满意。
• [fernly] 将该平台与Claude Projects进行比较。
• [scottward] 希望平台能自动同步Google Docs等源材料，而不仅依赖手动下载和上传。
• [argestes] 表示希望加入更新邮件列表。
• [tapeo] 分享了自己解决从聊天到聊天复制粘贴问题的经验，并提到现在可以生成基础上下文。
• [esafak] 认为用户界面看起来类似于You.com。

补充讨论：
• 隐私和安全是用户关注的重要问题，尤其是涉及上传工作相关数据时。
• 自动同步功能被一些用户视为关键需求。
• 用户对现有工具和解决方案的依赖以及对转换平台的抵触情绪是该类产品推广时需要考虑的因素。
• 不同用户对费用结构和商业模式有不同的看法和期望。
• 平台的差异化和附加功能（如对话分支、自动同步等）是吸引用户的关键。

data.title: Types of optical systems in a lens designer's toolbox (2020)
data.author: picture
data.article_summary: 这篇文章是一份关于镜头设计形式的终极指南，涵盖了各种光学系统及其应用。文章探讨了基本和重要的镜头设计形式，包括单透镜、双透镜、三合透镜、天塞透镜、双高斯透镜等，并解释了它们的发展和用途。文章还讨论了现代镜头设计，如非球面镜头、自由曲面镜头和用于手机摄像头的镜头，以及特殊用途的镜头系统，如鱼眼镜头、变焦镜头和反射光学镜头。此外，文章提供了对镜头设计背后原理的深入理解，帮助读者在面对规格表时更好地选择和设计镜头。文章最后还提到使用计算软件进行镜头设计的现代方法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：光学镜头设计工具和资源

不同观点：
• [alexbock] 提供了一个免费且开源的网页用户界面（UI），用于镜头设计，支持模拟双高斯镜头等设计。该工具允许用户操作镜头参数并观察效果，适合希望动手实验的用户。
• [Xmd5a] 提到了一个针对非专业人士的指南，指出该指南不适合那些愿意成为镜头设计“狂热者”的人。此外，Xmd5a 分享了自己在近红外光谱仪项目中通过试错法确定柱面镜最佳位置的经验，而没有进行严格的计算。
• [contingencies] 推荐了一本关于大画幅相机技术的书《View Camera Technique: 7th Edition》，认为其插图精美且内容有趣。此外，分享了在东莞遇到的从事iPhone镜头组装工作的韩国专家，指出高端镜头组装涉及多达13个镜片元素，每个组件都需要根据其具体光学特性进行数字化校正。
• [joshvm] 表达了对使用Mathematica中的Optica插件进行光学设计的兴趣，但指出该插件价格高昂，且很少遇到使用该工具的人，尽管学术界通常可以免费获得Mathematica。
• [elikoga] 提到了一个与“Torch Lens Maker”相关的项目，这是一个基于PyTorch的可微分几何光学工具，适合对光学模拟感兴趣的开发者。
• [NKosmatos] 试图寻找一个曾经使用过的镜头和光源模拟器，但未能找到相关链接，寻求社区帮助以找到该资源。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的工具和资源包括免费开源的网页工具、书籍推荐、商业软件插件以及基于Python的开发工具，展示了不同用户在镜头设计中的多样化需求和方法。
• 争议的焦点可能在于工具的获取和使用成本，例如Mathematica插件的高价让一些用户望而却步，而免费开源工具则更受欢迎。
• 用户分享了实际项目中的经验（如Xmd5a的试错法）以及行业专家的实践（如contingencies提到的iPhone镜头组装），为讨论增加了实际应用的视角。

Motivation and introduction to the General Theme
As an optical lens designer, there were times I used to think that “I can get the performance that I need for this system with the software, but I want to understand what I am doing”.

Zema

data.author: felineflock
data.article_summary: Chloe Lee研究了如何通过化学修饰乙酰氨基酚（扑热息痛）分子中的苯环来降低其对肝脏的毒性，同时保持其镇痛效果。乙酰氨基酚是广泛使用的止痛药，但也是美国急性肝衰竭的主要原因。Chloe利用计算机模型设计并合成了一种改良的乙酰氨基酚分子，该分子可能具有更低的毒性和更高的镇痛效力。她的研究为开发更安全、更有效的乙酰氨基酚形式提供了初步基础。此外，Chloe还是一名获奖的小提琴手，积极参与多项音乐和社区服务活动。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：评论围绕科学新闻杂志、乙酰氨基酚（acetaminophen）的疗效与安全性、青年科学人才的成就以及药物开发的可行性展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 一些评论对科学新闻杂志表示赞赏，如NortySpock分享了其父亲的订阅经历，强调了该杂志在科学报道方面的质量。
• 乙酰氨基酚的安全性与疗效成为讨论焦点。porphyra和foxwolf表示乙酰氨基酚的疗效不显著且有潜在的肝毒性问题，尤其是在饮酒的情况下。foxwolf还分享了个人使用该药物的经验，指出其在长期使用中的效果变化。
• 有关青年科学成就，Mizza、ItsHarper和djtango对17岁作者在科学项目中的表现表示赞赏。djtango特别强调了该项目的化学合成水平，并对其未来的学术发展表示期待。
• throwawaymaths则对该项目的创新性提出质疑，认为该项目主要是对已有药物的保护基团进行修改，并指出缺乏实验验证。

补充讨论：
• nandomrumber提出是否可以通过将乙酰氨基酚与N-乙酰半胱氨酸包装在一起来降低其肝毒性风险。
• CommenterPerson以讽刺口吻评论科学成就，提到自己的孩子在中学时“发现”了暗物质。
• snibsnib关注药物开发的经济性，质疑复杂合成反应是否会导致产品价格过高。
• aethrum提到了Antibe Therapeutics公司，可能是对药物开发领域的一个类比。
• neves简单指出乙酰氨基酚在不同地区的名称差异，并对帖子的高投票数表示不解。
• mewse-hn关注该项目是否已被Regeneron公司申请专利。

争议焦点：
• 乙酰氨基酚的疗效与安全性是主要争议点，部分评论者基于个人经验对其有效性提出质疑，而其他人则关注其潜在的毒性问题。
• 另一个争议点在于青年科学项目的创新性和实际应用价值，throwawaymaths认为项目创新不足，而其他人如djtango则高度评价其技术水平。

44077850.article_content:
Chemical Modification of Acetaminophen To Reduce Liver Toxicity and Enhance Drug Efficacy
Chloe studied ways to reduce the toxicity of acetaminophen while keeping its painkilling properties.
View Poster
Chloe Lee
View Poster
Chloe Yehwon Lee, 17, of Murphy, explored a way to lower the toxic effects of acetaminophen (Tylenol) on the liver for her Regeneron Science Talent Search chemistry project. The painkiller is used by over 60 million Americans each week, but it is also the leading cause of acute liver failure in the United States and the second most common cause of liver transplant worldwide. Chloe studied chemical changes to the acetaminophen molecule’s benzene ring to see if they could reduce liver toxicity.
Chloe studied chemical changes to the acetaminophen molecule’s benzene ring to see if they could reduce liver toxicity. She developed computer models of the modified molecules to test their ability to relieve pain and toxic effects. She found and synthesized a modified acetaminophen molecule that may be less toxic and may even kill pain better than the original. Her new molecule could be a first step in creating safer and more effective forms of acetaminophen.
Society for Science/Chris Ayers Photography
Chloe is the child of Jiyong Lee and Eul Hyun Suh. At Plano East Senior High School, she is president of the school’s orchestra program and first violinist in the Greater Dallas Youth Orchestra. She is also the founder and president of her school’s Girls in STEM club.
Society for Science/Chris Ayers Photography
Beyond the Project
Chloe is an award-winning violinist who performs with multiple orchestras. She has taught violin to younger students and plays with her school’s Ensembles for Elderly, which performs at assisted living and memory care centers.

data.title: Mermaid: Generation of diagrams like flowcharts or sequence diagrams from text
data.author: olalonde
data.article_summary: Mermaid 是一个基于 JavaScript 的图表和图形生成工具，允许用户使用类似 Markdown 的文本创建各种图表（如流程图、序列图和甘特图）。其主要目标是通过简化图表创建过程，解决文档与开发进度不匹配的问题，帮助开发人员节省时间，并保持文档的实时更新。Mermaid 支持通过 Live Editor 实时编辑和预览图表，并可以集成到生产脚本和各种应用程序（包括 GitHub）中。它还提供了丰富的文档、示例和教程，方便用户快速上手，并通过自动视觉回归测试确保图表质量。Mermaid 获得了 2019 年 JS 开源奖的“技术最激动人心的使用”奖项。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Mermaid及其他图表生成工具的应用与比较

不同观点：
• **支持Mermaid的观点**：
  - **herol3oy**：使用Mermaid生成书籍故事的关系图，提供项目链接。
  - **NightMKoder**：认为Mermaid很棒，尤其是因为有接近所见即所得的编辑器和Notion支持内联图表，方便工程文档的架构图展示。
  - **LifeIsBio**：赞赏Multimodal LLMs和Mermaid结合的工作流，可以通过手绘图生成Mermaid图表，极大提高了工作效率。
  - **paul_h**：使用Mermaid生成序列图，结合GPT4o提高了工作效率，但提到需要手动调整和追踪PNG文件的变化。
  - **wadewatts**：赞赏Mermaid图表简单易用，尤其在架构设计中生成多种图表。
  - **ding444**：在Obsidian中使用Mermaid，快速制作笔记中的图表，尤其在数据库表概念化时非常有用。
  - **iammrpayments**：认为Mermaid比excalidraw更流畅，尤其在处理大型图表时。

• **反对或提出替代方案的观点**：
  - **ris**：更喜欢d2，认为其设计更好，但没有浏览器内渲染器。
  - **smurpy**：推荐Kroki，支持多种文本驱动图表生成工具，包括Mermaid。
  - **ngm7**：提到excalidraw，认为其在传达想法时非常有用，尤其是可以导出到json，并提到有库可以将Mermaid转换为excalidraw。
  - **cogogo**：认为Mermaid现实应用不足，且已经存在很长时间。
  - **jagged-chisel**：询问Mermaid是否类似于PlantUML。
  - **kacesensitive**：推荐DiagramGPT，认为其体验很好。

• **争议焦点**：
  - **Mermaid vs. 其他工具（如d2、excalidraw、PlantUML、Graphviz等）**：不同用户对Mermaid的评价不一，有的用户认为其语法严格、设计不如Graphviz，但也有用户赞赏其在GitHub等平台上的便捷性。
  - **工具的功能与易用性**：一些用户关注工具的性能（如excalidraw的卡顿问题）和功能扩展（如k8s命名空间的 grouping）。

补充讨论：
- **工具集成与应用场景**：Mermaid被广泛应用于各种平台和工具中，如GitHub、Notion、Obsidian等，满足不同用户的图表生成需求。
- **AI结合**：Multimodal LLMs与Mermaid结合的工作流提高了复杂管道设计的效率，展示了AI在图表生成中的潜力。
- **用户体验**：不同用户对工具的界面、操作方式、性能等方面有不同偏好，反映出工具选择的多样性和个性化需求。

About
Mermaid is a JavaScript-based diagramming and charting tool that uses Markdown-inspired text definitions and a renderer to create and modify complex diagrams. The main purpose of Mermaid is to help documentation catch up with development.
Doc-Rot is a Catch-22 that Mermaid helps to solve.
Diagramming and documentation costs precious developer time and gets outdated quickly.
But not having diagrams or docs ruins productivity and hurts organizational learning.
Mermaid addresses this problem by enabling users to create easily modifiable diagrams. It can also be made part of production scripts (and other pieces of code).
Mermaid allows even non-programmers to easily create detailed diagrams through the
Mermaid Live Editor
.
For video tutorials, visit our

page.

.

applitools

  - **ding444**：在Obsidian中使用Mermaid，快速制作笔记中的图表，尤其在数据库表概念化时非常有用。
  - **iammrpayments**：认为Mermaid比excalidraw更流畅，尤其在处理大型图表时。

• **反对或提出替代方案的观点**：
  - **ris**：更喜欢d2，认为其设计更好，但没有浏览器内渲染器。
  - **smurpy**：推荐Kroki，支持多种文本驱动图表生成工具，包括Mermaid。
  - **ngm7**：提到excalidraw，认为其在传达想法时非常有用，尤其是可以导出到json，并提到有库可以将Mermaid转换为excalidraw。
  - **cogogo**：认为Mermaid现实应用不足，且已经存在很长时间。
  - **jagged-chisel**：询问Mermaid是否类似于PlantUML。
  - **kacesensitive**：推荐DiagramGPT，认为其体验很好。

• **争议焦点**：
  - **Mermaid vs. 其他工具（如d2、excalidraw、PlantUML、Graphviz等）**：不同用户对Mermaid的评价不一，有的用户认为其语法严格、设计不如Graphviz，但也有用户赞赏其在GitHub等平台上的便捷性。
  - **工具的功能与易用性**：一些用户关注工具的性能（如excalidraw的卡顿问题）和功能扩展（如k8s命名空间的 grouping）。

补充讨论：
- **工具集成与应用场景**：Mermaid被广泛应用于各种平台和工具中，如GitHub、Notion、Obsidian等，满足不同用户的图表生成需求。
- **AI结合**：Multimodal LLMs与Mermaid结合的工作流提高了复杂管道设计的效率，展示了AI在图表生成中的潜力。
- **用户体验**：不同用户对工具的界面、操作方式、性能等方面有不同偏好，反映出工具选择的多样性和个性化需求。

data.author: ecliptik
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：PC-98计算机的历史、技术特点及其在不同领域的应用和影响

不同观点：
• TD-Linux认为文章中展示的游戏大多不是同人游戏，而是商业出版物。他还指出PC-98未在美国销售，因此在美国不为人知，但在日本却是80年代末到90年代初最流行的计算机，拥有大量软件支持，包括办公软件和游戏。
• sombragris分享了个人经历，提到在大学期间见过NEC PC 9801用于植物标本的登记工作，并对其文本显示效果印象深刻。
• mrandish对文章中将“PC-98”描述为一种独特的像素艺术风格表示怀疑，但承认日本计算机由于需要显示更复杂的字体，可能在图形能力上有其独特性。他还指出，日本计算机更早使用模拟RGB输出，这可能导致其像素艺术在显示效果上的独特性。
• rollcat通过FreeBSD发布历史引出PC-98的技术支持问题，认为其类似于当前Arm架构所面临的标准化问题。

补充讨论：
• theogravity推荐了YouTube频道Basement Brothers，其中有关于PC-88和PC-98游戏的回顾和历史背景。
• makeitdouble提到了一部与PC-98时代相关的轻小说或动漫《16bit sensation》。
• krispyfi纠正了关于游戏《Policenauts》的描述，认为应为《Snatcher》。
• tempodox对PC-98的色彩表现给予高度评价，认为优于同时期的DOS电脑。
• jovial_cavalier对讨论中分享的成人内容表示不满，认为应保持专业性。
• ngcc_hk提到PC-98可以运行在DOSBox-X上，并讨论了其收藏的计算器以及对日本老式科学计算器的兴趣。

争议焦点：
• PC-98是否可以被称为一种独特的像素艺术风格及其技术特点的讨论。
• 讨论中出现的成人内容分享是否合适的争议。

data.title: Show HN: High-resolution surface analysis with Lidar data
data.author: folli
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了使用LiDAR数据进行高分辨率地表分析的项目“delta-relief”。该项目基于瑞士联邦地形局（Swisstopo）提供的swissALTI3D数据，通过移除建筑物和植被揭示底层地形。数据以GeoTIFF格式提供，每个图块代表1平方公里，分辨率为0.5米。项目目标包括将数据可视化为图像以突出细微地形变化，并部署为互动式、移动端友好的在线地图。目前，部分数据已在网上开放，用户可以查看LiDAR、航拍和地图视图三种图层。文章还介绍了通过LiDAR发现的历史遗迹，如罗马营地和青铜时代聚落，并讨论了如何有效地可视化这些数据。技术细节包括使用灰度梯度和高光阴影来呈现地形特征。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LiDAR技术在考古学和地形变化检测中的应用及其局限性

不同观点：
• weinzierl认为，移除植被以揭示地形是可理解的，但对如何移除建筑物表示疑惑，并询问实现这一操作的具体方法。
• schobi对描述中提到的利用LiDAR测量检测地形“变化”感到困惑，认为这种变化不可能是时间上的前后对比，尤其是在用于探测中世纪遗迹时。他推测这种变化更可能是通过可视化代码来突出自然与人工建筑结构之间的差异，而非用于发现新的遗迹。
• lyu07282引用了LiDAR在考古学中的成功应用案例（如Caspari, 2023），强调该技术能够揭示隐藏在植被或微小地形变化下的古代道路、墙体、建筑基础等结构，并提到亚马逊城市遗迹的发现也是得益于LiDAR技术。

补充讨论：
• schobi对LiDAR技术是否能够帮助发现新的考古遗址表示怀疑，认为它更适合于已知地点的可视化处理。
• lyu07282对LiDAR技术的潜力表示乐观，并指出该技术在考古学中的实际应用案例，如亚马逊城市的发现。
• 争议焦点在于LiDAR技术在考古学中用于发现新遗址的有效性。schobi对此持怀疑态度，而lyu07282则持积极看法。

总结：讨论围绕LiDAR技术在考古学中的应用展开，重点在于其对地形变化的检测能力以及在发现新考古遗址方面的潜力。不同的观点集中在该技术的实际效果和应用范围上。

delta-relief
High-resolution surface analysis with LiDAR data
Introduction
Airborne LiDAR uses hundreds of thousands of laser pulses per second to generate detailed 3D maps, even through vegetation.
With high point densities and 10 cm accuracy, it is among the most effective methods for mapping topography.
Source
SwissTopo
The Swiss Federal Office of Topography (Swisstopo) provides a highly precise digital elevation model based on LiDAR data,
called
swissALTI3D
. Buildings and vegetation are removed, revealing
the underlying topography.
The data is delivered as a GeoTIFF tiles with 2000px × 2000px resolution representing 1km × 1km areas (resolution of 0.5m).
The full list of all tiles is provided
here
.
Note
Swisstopo uses the
Swiss coordinates system LV95
, aka. EPSG:2056.
LiDAR has some interesting use cases in archaeology (
Caspari, 2023
),
particularly for uncovering man-made structures that are hidden beneath vegetation or subtle terrain changes.
It allows archaeologists to identify features such as ancient roads, walls, building foundations, and agricultural
terraces that may be invisible to the naked eye or conventional aerial photography.
Goal of this Project
This project aims to improve accessibility to the data in two main steps:
Visualize the SwissTopo data as images that highlight subtle terrain changes for easier interpretation
Deploy the data in an interactive, mobile-friendly online map
Currently, part of this data of eastern Switzerland (North Graubünden) is accessible on
https://lidar.cubetrek.com
The online map allows to quickly pan to the current location via GPS and switch between three different map layers
(LiDAR, this project; Aerial View and Map View, data from SwissTopo).
Points of Interest
Some examples of interesting features in the covered area (North Graubünden).
Note
Help me extend this list! Send a pull request or mail to:
contact@cubetrek.com
if
you know of any other interesting examples.
See also the Jupyter Notebook (
delta-relief-notebook.ipynb
) for more examples in other places of Switzerland.
Colm La Runga
Remains of a roman camp sitting at an altitude of 2200 m ASL. Likely around 15 BC, marking the start of the Roman occupation of this area of the Alps.
The camp was discovered in 2024, and was partly an inspiration of this project, as LiDAR data was also used to help in the discovery.
Sources:
Picture source:
Kanton Graubünden
Swiss Info: Remains of Roman camp discovered in eastern Switzerland
Swiss Info: Swiss Roman battle site reveals hidden secrets of historic clash
Rohanschanze (Rohan's fortification)
Built during the Thirty Years' War (1635) by the French Duke of Rohan. Only the earthwork remains.
Sources:
Burgenverein Untervaz, PDF, German
Rohanschanze, Wikipedia, German
Cresta Settlement in Cazis
Bronze Age settlement situated on a hilltop, the settlement was continuously inhabited for approximately 500 to 600 years
during the Early to Middle Bronze Age (circa 2000–1300 BCE).
Excavations have uncovered multiple layers of occupation, revealing structures such as post-built houses, hearths, and storage pits.
Sources:
Sonderheft Archäologischer Dienst Graubünden, PDF, German
Cresta-Siedlung, Wikipedia, German
Technical Details
Visualization of LiDAR data
The figures below are created in the
Visualization trials Jupyter Notebook
.
To demonstrate how to display subtle terrain changes in the best way, we use two examples:
the Rohanschanze on the left illustrates clearly visible earthworks in flat terrain, while the
Colm La Runga on the right highlights more subtle features in a mountainous landscape.
The input data consists of absolute elevation values (height above sea level). A basic way to visualize this is as a
grayscale gradient-black representing the lowest and white the highest altitude within each tile.
While the fort is visible, the Roman camp gets completely lost in the surrounding mountainous terrain.
n scientific visualizations, elevation data is often rendered using
hillshading
.
This produces a natural-looking terrain representation, but it requires significant tuning to make subtle features

data.title: Rork – Build any cross-platform mobile app, fast
data.author: colesantiago
data.article_summary: Rork是一个利用AI和React Native构建跨平台移动应用的平台，能够快速开发多种类型的应用程序。它提供的功能包括制作视觉小说游戏、类似Airbnb的预订应用、类似Instagram的社交应用、冥想计时器、习惯追踪器、卡路里追踪器、待办事项列表、天气仪表盘和健身追踪器等。Rork旨在简化应用开发流程，帮助用户高效创建各种移动应用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对Rork平台的体验和评价，涉及功能、价格、实用性以及局限性。

data.title: Why Algebraic Effects?
data.author: jiggawatts
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了代数效应（algebraic effects）的用途和优势，特别是它们在编程语言中的应用。代数效应允许用户定义控制流，并可以作为库来实现多种语言特性，如生成器、异常、协程等。它们通过效应处理器（effect handlers）实现，类似于可恢复的异常。文章展示了如何使用代数效应实现诸如异常、生成器等功能，并强调了它们在创建更清洁API、替代全局变量、保证纯函数以及能力安全（capability-based security）方面的优势。作者以Ante语言为例，通过伪代码演示了效应的声明、抛出和捕获过程，并解释了效应的多态性在函数签名中的应用。总体而言，代数效应提供了一种强大且灵活的编程范式，有助于解决多种编程问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： algebraic effects的概念、优缺点及其在实际应用中的可行性

不同观点：
• **nemo1618**：提出两个主要缺点。首先，函数签名没有明确指示可能失败的操作（如`foo`和`bar`），需要查找类型签名或借助IDE。其次，错误处理代码难以定位，因为错误处理可能在多个调用栈上层，且无法静态跳转。
• **carterschonwald**：希望能有局部声明某些效果为隐式的代数效应，使其在类型中不可见。
• **huqedato**：赞赏Ante语言的表达能力和实用性，期待其编译器的成熟。
• **evelant**：认为无需新语言即可实现代数效应，如TypeScript中的effect库，且该库已成熟并用于生产环境。
• **aatd86**：对代数效应的概念感到困惑，质疑某些效果是否是任意决定的，以及这些是否仅仅是副作用操作的符号化表示。
• **AdieuToLogic**：认为代数效应类似于现有的ApplicativeError或MonadError类型类，质疑其新颖性和独特性，并指出代数效应已经在当今语言中存在。
• **practal**：对代数效应感兴趣，但因其通常与静态类型系统相关而不愿深入研究，并提出动态类型的可能性。
• **cdaringe**：曾使用OCaml 5的效果功能，认为其有趣但工具链尚不成熟，期待其进展。
• **nevertoolate**：质疑代数效应是否会被主流语言采用，担心其引入的抽象概念可能导致团队开发中的混乱。
• **wild_egg**：将代数效应与Common Lisp的条件系统相比较，认为这是旧概念的新命名。
• **michalsustr**：关注代数效应在大型项目中的可用性，特别是调试时的“跳跃”问题，担心导致代码难以理解和维护。
• **nikita2206**：认为生成器（generators）比异常更接近代数效应，首次了解此概念时便觉得其显而易见。
• **rixed**：对代数效应的广泛应用持怀疑态度，认为其类似于动态作用域，可能带来痛苦的经验。
• **yyyk**：对状态效果的例子提出疑问，质疑是否需要在每个函数中重复效果声明，建议使用类型或命名空间进行分组。
• **xixixao**：认为代数效应强大但担心依赖注入的缺点，倾向于在测试环境中“覆盖”具体实现而非在非测试代码中失去静态调用关系。

补充讨论：
• 代数效应的可读性和可调试性是争议焦点，特别是错误处理代码的定位和在大型项目中的维护难度。
• 不同开发者对代数效应的实际应用和在主流语言中的可行性持不同看法，有人期待其成熟应用，有人担心其引入的复杂性。
• 对代数效应的理解和接受程度因开发者的背景和经验而异，静态类型与动态类型的讨论也是重要方面。

Why Algebraic Effects
Algebraic effects
1
(a.k.a. effect handlers) are a very useful up-and-coming feature that I personally think will see a huge surge in popularity in the programming
languages of tomorrow. They’re one of the core features of Ante, as well as being the focus of many research
languages including
Koka
,
Effekt
,
Eff
,
and
Flix
. However, while many articles or documentation snippets try to explain
what
effect handlers are (including
Ante’s own documentation
), few really go in-depth on
why
you would want to use them.
In this post I’ll explain exactly that and will include as complete a list as possible on all the use-cases of algebraic effects.
A Note on Syntax and Semantics
I’ll be using Ante pseudocode for much of this article. If you’re not familiar with effect handlers or Ante I encourage you to read the documentation link
above or read from any of the other effectful languages for a good head start! But I recognize it’s hard to get buy-in to learn something before showing
why it is useful first (hence this blog post!). So I’ll give a quick elevator pitch on a good mental model to think about effects.
You can think of algebraic effects essentially as exceptions that you can resume. You can declare an effect function:
effect
SayMessage
with
// This effect function takes a Unit type and returns a Unit type.
// Note that `Unit` is roughly the same as `void` in imperative languages.
// There are differences between them but none that are relevant here.
say_message
:
Unit
->
Unit
You can “throw” an effect by calling the function, and the function you’re in must declare it can use that effect similar to checked exceptions:
foo
()
can
SayMessage
=
say_message
()
42
And you can “catch” effects with a
handle
expression (think of these as
try/catch
expressions):
handle
foo
()
|
say_message
()
->
print
"Hello World!"
// print out Hello World!
resume
()
// then resume the computation, returning 42
If you have further questions I again encourage you to read
some documentation
on effects, but now
that we can recognize effects when they’re used I’ll get into why exactly the idea of exceptions-you-can-resume are so useful!
User-defineable control-flow
The most common reason you’ll hear for why to have effect handlers is that they are a single language feature which
allow for implementing what would normally be multiple separate language features (generators, exceptions, async, coroutines, etc)
as libraries. Moreover, they solve the
what color is your function
problem by making functions polymorphic over effects. For example, a
map
function for vectors (growable arrays) can be written once:
map
(
input
:
Vec
a
)
(
f
:
a
->
b
can
e
)
:
Vec
b
can
e

44078434.article_summary: 本文讨论了代数效应（algebraic effects）的用途和优势，特别是它们在编程语言中的应用。代数效应允许用户定义控制流，并可以作为库来实现多种语言特性，如生成器、异常、协程等。它们通过效应处理器（effect handlers）实现，类似于可恢复的异常。文章展示了如何使用代数效应实现诸如异常、生成器等功能，并强调了它们在创建更清洁API、替代全局变量、保证纯函数以及能力安全（capability-based security）方面的优势。作者以Ante语言为例，通过伪代码演示了效应的声明、抛出和捕获过程，并解释了效应的多态性在函数签名中的应用。总体而言，代数效应提供了一种强大且灵活的编程范式，有助于解决多种编程问题。
44078434.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： algebraic effects的概念、优缺点及其在实际应用中的可行性

不同观点：
• **nemo1618**：提出两个主要缺点。首先，函数签名没有明确指示可能失败的操作（如`foo`和`bar`），需要查找类型签名或借助IDE。其次，错误处理代码难以定位，因为错误处理可能在多个调用栈上层，且无法静态跳转。
• **carterschonwald**：希望能有局部声明某些效果为隐式的代数效应，使其在类型中不可见。
• **huqedato**：赞赏Ante语言的表达能力和实用性，期待其编译器的成熟。
• **evelant**：认为无需新语言即可实现代数效应，如TypeScript中的effect库，且该库已成熟并用于生产环境。
• **aatd86**：对代数效应的概念感到困惑，质疑某些效果是否是任意决定的，以及这些是否仅仅是副作用操作的符号化表示。
• **AdieuToLogic**：认为代数效应类似于现有的ApplicativeError或MonadError类型类，质疑其新颖性和独特性，并指出代数效应已经在当今语言中存在。
• **practal**：对代数效应感兴趣，但因其通常与静态类型系统相关而不愿深入研究，并提出动态类型的可能性。
• **cdaringe**：曾使用OCaml 5的效果功能，认为其有趣但工具链尚不成熟，期待其进展。
• **nevertoolate**：质疑代数效应是否会被主流语言采用，担心其引入的抽象概念可能导致团队开发中的混乱。
• **wild_egg**：将代数效应与Common Lisp的条件系统相比较，认为这是旧概念的新命名。
• **michalsustr**：关注代数效应在大型项目中的可用性，特别是调试时的“跳跃”问题，担心导致代码难以理解和维护。
• **nikita2206**：认为生成器（generators）比异常更接近代数效应，首次了解此概念时便觉得其显而易见。
• **rixed**：对代数效应的广泛应用持怀疑态度，认为其类似于动态作用域，可能带来痛苦的经验。
• **yyyk**：对状态效果的例子提出疑问，质疑是否需要在每个函数中重复效果声明，建议使用类型或命名空间进行分组。
• **xixixao**：认为代数效应强大但担心依赖注入的缺点，倾向于在测试环境中“覆盖”具体实现而非在非测试代码中失去静态调用关系。

补充讨论：
• 代数效应的可读性和可调试性是争议焦点，特别是错误处理代码的定位和在大型项目中的维护难度。
• 不同开发者对代数效应的实际应用和在主流语言中的可行性持不同看法，有人期待其成熟应用，有人担心其引入的复杂性。
• 对代数效应的理解和接受程度因开发者的背景和经验而异，静态类型与动态类型的讨论也是重要方面。

data.title: Show HN: Web Apps for Python Devs with Auto-Generated UI
data.author: ruben-davia
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种快速构建自定义工具的方法——使用Davia平台，从数据和Python代码出发，无需前端开发即可创建交互式工具。Davia自动将Python代码转化为带有直观界面的全功能工具，支持集成现有Python代码、API和数据源，跳过复杂的UI设计。用户可在几分钟内构建、发布和分享工具，通过简单链接让团队即时访问和使用，而无需复杂安装。Davia基于FastAPI，提供一键部署和安全托管。文章还列举了多个应用案例，如管理仪表盘、数据清理工具、数据可视化仪表盘、库存管理系统、自动化报告工具和邮件发送工具。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Devia（或类似工具）的功能、使用体验及技术实现细节

不同观点：
• Jerpint认为Devia的代码装饰器功能和FastAPI集成非常有用，并建议可以作为一个独立功能在云端或边缘函数服务中运行，以增强其实用性。
• Djaychela对网站的用户体验提出不满，特别提到视频自动播放问题，认为应让用户自行决定何时播放视频。
• Vladdoster对演示视频中的技术实现提出疑问，具体包括为何使用OPTIONS和POST两次请求而不是单次GET请求，以及为何使用POST请求获取销售数据，而非更常见的GET请求。
• Ashishb希望了解Devia相比Gradio和Streamlit有哪些独特的功能或优势。
• Rohitcss同样对自动播放视频表示不满，建议使用GIF代替，以改善用户体验。
• Qwertox质疑为何查看“用例示例”需要先注册，认为这种设计可能对用户不友好。

补充讨论：
• 技术实现细节：Vladdoster对请求方法的选择提出了具体的技术质疑，表明开发者在实现过程中可能需要更多考虑请求方法的合理性。
• 用户体验问题：Djaychela和Rohitcss都提到视频自动播放的问题，表明这是一个较普遍的用户体验痛点。
• 功能对比：Ashishb强调了对Devia独特功能的期待，表明用户在选择工具时会比较不同工具之间的功能差异。
• 隐私与访问权限：Qwertox对查看内容需要注册的要求提出质疑，涉及到用户隐私和访问便捷性的讨论。

争议焦点：
• 视频自动播放的设计是否合理：Djaychela和Rohitcss都对此表示不满，建议改进。
• 请求方法的技术合理性：Vladdoster对演示视频中请求方法的选择提出疑问，表明在技术实现上存在争议。
• 注册查看内容的必要性：Qwertox质疑需要注册才能查看用例的设计，涉及到用户隐私和便捷性之间的平衡。

44078813.article_content:
W
hen people
ask what I do for a living, I’m faced with two choices: either I can lie or I can bore them with the truth, which is too complicated to explain succinctly. While those around me have normal, definable jobs—accountant, journalist, engineer—my work requires headings and subheadings to get it across properly: a map of overlapping gigs and contracts.
“What do you do?” It’s a simple question that often gets asked on first dates. No matter how much I pare down my reply, it’s always long winded.
“Well, I’m a freelancer,” I start, “so I have a million little jobs . . .”
The first of my million little jobs is what I call “Horse News.” It works like this: every weekday, I wake up at 6 a.m. and make my way to my desk, stumbling and still half asleep. I flick on an old lamp and wince as my eyes adjust to the light. I turn on my computer and use a piece of software that shows me all of the American horse racing–related news from the past twenty-four hours. It pulls up radio clips, Fox News segments, and articles from publications called
BloodHorse
or
Daily Racing Form
—anything that could be relevant to my interests.
I sift through countless story summaries, many of which sound fake.
Army Wife defeats Crazy Beautiful Woman in race! Another doping scandal emerges in Northern California! A disgraced-but-very-good trainer is no longer banned from the track! A famous YouTuber has invested millions into a betting app!
I compile the important stuff into a newsletter: stories about track renovations, big events, the series of horse laws that were passed, then repealed, then approved again in 2023.
This is a true, real thing. These laws (known as the Horseracing Integrity and Safety Act) are meant to keep racehorses and jockeys safer. Tracks are required to provide on-site vets and doctors and to follow standardized safety protocols. But it is much cheaper, it turns out, to ignore the laws and have the horses race in dangerous conditions. Vets and safety gear are expensive, which is upsetting to the billionaires who own the racetracks. And so certain states have fought these laws, calling them unconstitutional. I have followed along, every step of the way.
In Defence of Garlic in a Jar: How Food Snobs Almost Ruined My Love of Cooking
Why Do I Constantly Have to Prove My Disability?
My Brief but Fruitful Career as a Smut Peddler
When the newsletter is finished, I send it to my client, a company that owns racetracks across the US. Though, to be clear, I don’t work for them directly. I work for a reputation management firm. This company’s entire purpose is to monitor the news for other companies, keeping tabs on what the public is saying about their clients and the major trends in those industries. I didn’t know this was a real job until I started doing it.
I got this job the way I’ve gotten most of my jobs: through an acquaintance who heard I was looking for work. This is key to success in freelancing. You just need to build a roster of industry connections who know how desperate you are.
“It’s just an hour per morning,” she told me. “Usually less.”
“Sure,” I said, still not understanding what I was agreeing to. “I’ll do it.”
The reputation management firm has a slew of different clients, each of whom wants a personalized newsletter about their industry. There’s a fast food chain, a brewery, an environmental organization. But I was assigned to the horse racing client. And so I keep up with Horse News and Horse Laws. By 7:30 a.m., the report is done, and I go back to bed.

不同观点：

• **mdaniel**对SweepIQ的商业模式提出质疑，通过一个假设情境指出：SweepIQ通过亚马逊联盟链接让用户购买产品，但AI工具本身（如GPU资源的使用）的成本如何覆盖没有解释清楚。
• **vouaobrasil**对加速学习持反对态度，认为学习不应以效率和生产力为导向，而应出于对知识的热爱。他担心过度自动化学习会剥夺学习过程中的美感和发现的乐趣。
• **kolpaque**对SweepIQ持较为积极的态度，认为它类似于Perplexity的工具，但免费且通过亚马逊联盟链接盈利。他指出SweepIQ有一些不错的功能，如后续问题和“像五岁孩子一样解释”的选项，但也存在保存和引用源方面的问题。
• **michaelbuckbee**提到谷歌有一个类似的工具叫"Learn About"，指出市场上有多种同类工具可供选择。
• **jeisc**具体测试了SweepIQ对特朗普的查询，发现只涵盖了其第一个任期，对内容的全面性提出质疑。
• **OdehAhwal**对该工具表示高度赞赏，认为它不仅适用于学习，还适合用于创意构思。

补充讨论：
• SweepIQ的**商业模式**（通过亚马逊联盟链接盈利）引起了一定的关注和质疑，尤其是AI工具如何负担自身运行成本的问题。
• **学习效率与学习态度**之间的争议：一部分用户（如creata）关注学习工具的效率和递进性，另一部分用户（如vouaobrasil）则强调学习本身应出于热爱，而不是单纯追求效率和生产力。
• 工具的**功能与不足**：kolpaque指出SweepIQ有不错的功能设计，但也有技术上的不足之处，如保存和引用源的功能不完善。

data.title: Not causal chains, but interactions and adaptations
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 作者Lorin Hochstein对根原因分析（RCA）持批评态度，认为其基于对复杂系统故障的错误理解。尽管英国健康与安全执行局（HSE）的《调查事故和事件》指南指出事故由多重原因引发，并强调不应将“人为错误”作为唯一原因，作者仍认为RCA的因果链模型（从根本原因到直接原因）在复杂系统中并不适用。作者反对将事故视为单一可预防事件，强调复杂系统中的故障通常由多个因素和偶然事件共同导致，RCA的简单因果模型无法有效预防未来事件。作者呼吁在软件领域应寻找更适合的分析方法，而不是依赖RCA。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对原文中关于潜在错误和容错机制的讨论，评论者们提出了对管理、技术实践以及类比方法的不同看法。

不同观点：
• [wduquette] 认为原文假设了管理层和制度上的根本原因已经解决，但实际情况中，一个不做单元测试、不消除技术债务的组织会产生更多明显的错误。他主张需要一种“兼顾”的方法，既解决表面错误，也关注潜在错误。

• [xg15] 部分同意原文观点，但认为原文缺乏具体的方法论例子。他通过森林火灾的类比说明，寻找火灾具体原因（如无人控制的营火或电线故障）对预防未来火灾帮助有限。他将讨论引向如何让个别火灾无法蔓延成灾，例如关注森林的整体健康状况，从而改变环境以防止火灾蔓延。

补充讨论：
• [xg15] 提出的类比认为，通过改变系统环境（如森林的干燥度和堆积物），可以防止小问题演变成大灾难。这种观点强调系统健康和环境因素的重要性，而不是只关注单个错误的根源。

• 争议的焦点在于是否应优先解决明显的技术问题（如单元测试）还是更应关注系统整体健康和容错能力。一方认为解决具体技术问题是前提，另一方则强调系统性预防和环境改造。

• 两者的共同点是都认识到潜在错误和管理问题的重要性，但在实施策略上存在分歧：一个主张具体问题具体解决，另一个则提倡系统性、环境性的预防策略。

44038686.article_content:
Lorin Hochstein
resilience
May 19, 2025
May 19, 2025
8 Minutes
I’ve been a bit of an anti-root-cause-analysis (RCA) tear lately. On LinkedIn, health and safety expert
Vincent Theobald-Vega
left a
thoughtful, detailed comment
on my last post. In his comment, he noted that RCA done poorly leads to bad results, and he pointed me to what he described as a good guide to using the RCA approach:
Investigating accidents and incidents
. This is a free book published by the UK
Health and Safety Executive
.
However, after reading this guide, my perception of RCA has not improved. I still believe that RCA is based on a fundamentally incorrect model of complex systems failure. To clarify my thinking, I’ve tried to explain where I see its flaws in this post.
A quick note on terminology: while the guide uses the term
accident
, I’m going to use the term
incident
instead, to remain consistent with the usage in the software domain. The guide uses incident to refer to near misses.
Some content in the guide that I appreciated
While I disagree with RCA as described in the guide, I wanted to start by pointing out areas of agreement I had with the guide.
Not just a single cause
The guide does note that there are multiple causes involved in incidents. It notes that
adverse events have many causes
(p6), and it also mentions that
Very often, a number of chance occurrences and coincidences combine to create the circumstances in which an adverse event can happen. All these factors should be recorded here in chronological order, if possible.
(p10).
While I disagree with the causal language, I do at least appreciate that it points out there are multiple factors.
Examine how work is really done
The guide does talk about examining the work and the context under which it takes place. Under “information and insights gained from an investigation”, one of the bullet points is
A true snapshot of what really happens and how work is really done
(p7).
Under the “Gathering detailed information: How and what? section, the guide asks
What activities were being carried out at the time?
and
Was there anything unusual or different about the working conditions?”
(p15)
“Human error” is not a valid conclusion
The guide is opposed to the idea of human error being identified as a cause. It notes that
Investigations that conclude that operator error was the sole cause are rarely acceptable. Underpinning the ‘human error’ there will be a number of underlying causes that created the environment in which human errors were inevitable
. (p10)
Examine your near misses
Finally, the guide does point out the value in investigating near misses, noting that
While the argument for investigating accidents is fairly clear, the need to investigate
near misses and undesired circumstances may not be so obvious. However, investigating near misses and undesired circumstances is as useful, and very much easier than investigating accidents.
(p8)
The RCA model of incidents
Here’s my attempt to sketch out a conceptual model of how incidents happened, according to the guide.
The guide distinguishes between three different types of causes:
Immediate cause
–
the most obvious reason why an adverse  event happens
(p4)
Underlying cause
–
the less obvious ‘system’ or ‘organisational’ reason for an adverse event happening
(p5)
Root cause – an initiating event or failing from which all other causes or failings spring
.
Root causes are generally management, planning or organisational failings
(p5).
How root causes lead to incidents
The idea is that there is a
causal chain
from root cause to underlying  cause to immediate cause. A combination of these immediate causes, along with chance occurrences and coincidences, combine to enable the incident.
The guide uses the metaphor of a sequence of dominos to describe this causal chain, where the initial domino (labeled “A” in the diagram below) is a root cause, and the domino labeled “B” an immediate cause.
Source: Investigating accidents and incidents, UK Health and Safety Executive, figure 4, p6
If left unaddressed, these root causes will lead to multiple incidents in the future. Hence, the goal of an RCA is to identify and eliminate the root causes in order to prevent recurrence of the incident:
The same accidents happen again and again
, causing suffering and distress to an ever-widening circle of workers and their families… The findings of the investigation will form the basis of an action plan
to prevent the accident or incident from happening again
…
(p4, emphasis mine)
To get rid of weeds you must dig up the root. If you only cut off the foliage, the weed will grow again. Similarly it is only by carrying out investigations
which identify root causes
that organisations can learn from their past failures and prevent future failures.
(p9, emphasis mine)
The RE model of incidents
My claim is that the RCA model of incidents is dangerously incorrect about the nature of failure in complex systems. More importantly, these flaws in the RCA model l

data.title: Stuff I Learned at Carta
data.author: blueridge
data.article_summary:
本文是作者作为Carta公司前CTO在离职之际对过去两年工作经验的总结。作者强调了几点主要收获：

1. **深入细节**：过去他习惯于高层次的抽象思考，而在Carta，深入细节以获取信息和推动进度成为领导风格的一部分。
2. **工程战略的 refinement**：作者撰写了一本关于工程战略的书，Carta提供了复杂的项目和优秀的人才来实践这些战略。
3. **提取核心**：学会从 executives 的沟通中提取关键信息，而不是仅仅抱怨沟通不清。
4. **采用LLMs**：Carta在业务流程中使用LLMs已有一年多，并计划推出新的产品功能。
5. **多维度权衡**：通过多维度权衡和多层次背景来改善复杂决策的质量。
6. **导航者计划**：推出Navigator计划，确保高级工程师有直接的代表性，而不仅依赖于工程管理的间接代表。
7. **软件质量**：认识到某些软件因“高本质复杂性”而难以构建，即使它们在基础设施扩展方面没有复杂性。
8. **塑造工程组织的成本**：通过“N-1 backfills”、为晋升到最高级别提供商业理由和将招聘转移到成本效率高的地区来管理工程薪资成本。

作者表示将在几周后公布他的新去向。

44078094.article_content:
Today’s my last day at Carta, where I got the chance to serve as their CTO
for the past two years. I’ve learned
so much
working there, and I wanted
to end my chapter there by collecting my thoughts on what I learned.
(I am heading somewhere, and will share news in a week or two after
firming up the communication plan with my new team there.)
The most important things I learned at Carta were:
Working in the details
–
if you took a critical lens towards my historical leadership style,
I think the biggest issue you’d point at is my being too comfortable operating at a high level of abstraction.
Utilizing the expertise of others to fill in your gaps is a valuable skill, but–like any single approach–it’s
limiting when utilized too frequently.
One of the strengths of Carta’s “house leadership style” is expecting leaders to
go deep into the details to get informed and push pace.
What I practiced there turned into the pieces on
strategy testing
and
developing domain expertise
.
Refining my approach to engineering strategy
–
over the past 18 months, I’ve written a book on engineering strategy
(posts are all in
#eng-strategy-book
),
with initial chapters coming available for early release with O’Reilly
next month. Fingers crossed, the book will be released in approximately October.
Coming into Carta, I already had
much
of my core thesis about how to do engineering strategy,
but Carta gave me a number of complex projects to practice on, and excellent people to
practice with: thank you to Dan, Shawna and Vogl in particular!
More on this project in the next few weeks.
Extract the kernel
–
everywhere I’ve ever worked, teams have struggled understanding executives.
In every case, the executives
could be clearer
, but it’s not particularly interesting
to frame these problems as something the executives need to fix.
Sure, that’s true they could communicate better, but that framing makes you powerless,
when you have a great deal of power to understand confusing communication.
After all, even good communicators communicate poorly sometimes.
Meaningfully adopting LLMs
–
a year ago I wrote up
notes on adopting LLMs in your products
,
based on what we’d learned so far. Since then, we’ve learned a lot more, and LLMs themselves have significantly improved.
Carta has been using LLMs in real, business-impacting workflows for over a year. That’s continuing to expand into
solving more complex internal workflows, and even more interestingly into creating net-new product capabilities that
ought to roll out more widely in the next few months (currently released to small beta groups).
This is the first major technology transition that I’ve experienced in a senior leadership role (since I
was earlier in my career when mobile internet transitioned from novelty to commodity).
The immense pressure to adopt faster, combined with the immense uncertainty if it’s a meaningful change or a brief blip
was a lot of fun, and
was the inspiration for this strategy document around LLM adoption
.
Multi-dimensional tradeoffs
–
a phrase that Henry Ward uses frequent is that “everyone’s right, just at a different altitude.”
That idea resonates with me, and meshes well with the ideas of
multi-dimensional tradeoffs
and
layers of context
that I find improve decision making for folks in roles
that require making numerous, complex decisions. Working at Carta, these ideas formalized from
something I intuited into something I could explain clearly.
Navigators
–
I think our most successful engineering strategy at Carta was rolling out the Navigator program,
which ensured senior-most engineers had context and direct representation, rather than relying
exclusively on indirect representation via engineering management.
Carta’s engineering managers are excellent, but there’s always something lost as discussions
extend across layers. The Navigator program probably isn’t a perfect fit for particularly small
companies, but I think any company with more than 100-150 engineers would benefit from something
along these lines.
How to create software quality
–
I’ve evolved my thinking about software quality quite a bit over time,
but Carta was particularly helpful in distinguishing why some pieces of
software are so hard to build despite having little-to-no scale from
a data or concurrency perspective. These systems, which I label as “high
essential complexity”, deserve more credit for their complexity,
even if they have little in the way of complexity from infrastructure scaling.
Shaping eng org costs
–
a few years ago, I wrote about
my mental model for managing infrastructure costs
.
At Carta, I got to refine my thinking about engineering salary costs,
with most of those ideas getting incorporated in the
Navigating Private Equity ownership
strategy,
and the
eng org seniority mix model
.
The three biggest levers are (1) “N-1 backfills”, (2) requiring a business rationale for promotions into senior-most levels, and
(3) shifting hiring into cost efficient hiring regions.
None of
44078094.article_summary:
本文是作者作为Carta公司前CTO在离职之际对过去两年工作经验的总结。作者强调了几点主要收获：

1. **深入细节**：过去他习惯于高层次的抽象思考，而在Carta，深入细节以获取信息和推动进度成为领导风格的一部分。
2. **工程战略的 refinement**：作者撰写了一本关于工程战略的书，Carta提供了复杂的项目和优秀的人才来实践这些战略。
3. **提取核心**：学会从 executives 的沟通中提取关键信息，而不是仅仅抱怨沟通不清。
4. **采用LLMs**：Carta在业务流程中使用LLMs已有一年多，并计划推出新的产品功能。
5. **多维度权衡**：通过多维度权衡和多层次背景来改善复杂决策的质量。
6. **导航者计划**：推出Navigator计划，确保高级工程师有直接的代表性，而不仅依赖于工程管理的间接代表。
7. **软件质量**：认识到某些软件因“高本质复杂性”而难以构建，即使它们在基础设施扩展方面没有复杂性。
8. **塑造工程组织的成本**：通过“N-1 backfills”、为晋升到最高级别提供商业理由和将招聘转移到成本效率高的地区来管理工程薪资成本。

作者表示将在几周后公布他的新去向。

data.title: On "Vibe Coding"
data.author: cratermoon
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了AI领域的新概念“Vibe Coding”，即利用AI代码助手根据问题描述生成代码，而无需深入思考软件架构或解决方案表达。这种方法被宣传为技术民主化和赋权个人，但作者认为这些说法过于简单化且具有误导性。软件开发不仅仅是编写代码，还涉及需求分析、理解问题领域、架构设计等复杂过程，且大部分问题实质上是社会问题，需要同理心和沟通。作者批评“Vibe Coding”忽视了软件开发的深层次复杂性和经验的重要性，认为这种趋势可能会导致误解和不良实践。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成代码工具的实际效果和使用体验

不同观点：
• AllegedAlec认为AI工具在处理新项目和简单任务时表现出色，但在复杂项目或现有代码库中表现不佳。他强调，AI工具需要在特定场景下使用，且对用户的精确指导有高度依赖。他还提到，行业内对新工具的态度存在两极分化，一部分人拒绝接受，另一部分人则过度依赖。

• nopelynopington分享了一次不成功的Replit使用体验。尽管AI生成的UI看起来专业且精致，但功能上存在问题，且在多次尝试修复后仍未解决问题。最终，他发现AI只是在一系列的“幻觉”中进行对话，并未真正接受用户输入。他提到，其他非代理式LLM（如Gemini或Claude）表现更好。

• theospeak对AI工具持积极态度，认为这些工具降低了开发门槛，使得更多人可以参与到“构建”过程中。他强调，开发者应该接受这种变化，并通过学习新技能来提高自己，而不是抱怨工具带来的改变。他个人通过与AI工具的互动学到了很多新知识，并享受这个过程。

• garylkz认为使用AI生成代码没有问题，但关键在于对代码质量的监督，这需要用户具备一定的领域知识。他指出，依赖AI并不意味着可以轻松完成所有工作，仍然需要具备一定的技能和判断力。

• cranberryturkey作为一个有30多年经验的软件工程师，表示AI和“vibe编码”使他成为了一个10倍程序员。他认为，关键在于 prompt 的技巧和调试能力，而这些能力需要对问题解决和架构设计有深入理解。他分享了自己在两周内发布了8个npm模块的经历，显示出对AI工具的高效利用。

补充讨论：
• AI工具在处理新项目和简单任务时的有效性得到了多位用户的肯定，但在复杂项目中的表现存在争议。
• 用户对AI工具的期望和实际体验之间存在差距，特别是在问题修复和对话交互方面。
• 行业内对AI工具的态度存在两极分化，一部分人拒绝接受新工具，另一部分人则过度依赖。
• 使用AI工具需要具备一定的领域知识和技能，以有效监督和提高代码质量。
• 个人经验和背景会影响对AI工具的看法和使用效果，有些用户通过AI工具获得了显著的效率提升。

44076771.article_content:
On “Vibe Coding”
May 23, 2025
—
by
tante
in
english
,
Writing
The hype about the potentials (it’s always future potential, never real current use) of AI has discarded its last cycle (“reasoning models”/”deep research”, both terms being factually untrue and deeply deceiving at best) and moved to a new double whammy of “agentic AI” and “Vibe Coding”.
Now “agentic AI” basically just means that some LLM starts calling random functions somewhere on the net
who needs security
in their architecture, right? But I want to look at the second part, now called “Vibe Coding”.
What prompted me writing this were a few distinct things. I gave a keynote yesterday at a corporate event where an internal tech evangelist did a whole thing on vibe coding (actually in a somewhat measured way, but it shows how strong the meme already is in the LinkedIn crowd) and a German “tech” influencer wrote a big thing in a big German magazine (not gonna link it, it’s just an ad for his keynote-business for LinkedIn people). But also serious people with some experience are starting to use the term.
“Vibe coding” refers to using an “AI” code assistant to write program code for you: Instead of thinking about software architecture or how to express your solution you basically just give a problem description and maybe fragments of a potential solution to an AI to generate the code for you. Especially if you are not familiar with the programming language you want to or need to use that obviously creates runnable code a lot faster than learning the whole new platform.
Narrative power
“Vibe coding” has a lot of narrative power. You can easily use it to put forth an argument about the “democratization of technology and software creation”, about “empowering individuals, groups and organizations to solve their own problems”, about “giving people access to the means of digital creation” etc. At first glance those narratives feel great, who doesn’t like “democratization”, “empowerment” and handing the means of production to the people? (That last one might not be everyone’s idea of a good time but it’s mine so let’s keep it here.)
But I think those narratives are massively underbaked at best and we don’t live in the best possible world so maybe we should call them short-sighted and deceiving if not just plain false. As with many digital narratives they don’t fully stand up to scrutiny but show a deep misunderstanding of how software is made, the potential externalities (and internalities) software brings and a disdain for experience and embodied knowledge.
Software
Software is a bit of a weird beast. Many people have a very wrong understanding what it is and how it is created. This is probably true for everything: We don’t know shit outside of our specific bubbles and that’s not bad in general because division of labor is – in my opinion – good. I like having specialists and experts on things tackle hard problems. But software has been shoved as an abstraction layer into so many of our systems, our social connections, our work, the way we interact with the world etc. Software is kinda everywhere and is a lot of the time the goto solution for any problem: Your office has problems with processes? Maybe buy another software tool to not write proper tickets and documentation in.
Software is kind of the meta solution to anything. Not a specific tool but the
way to think
about tools and solutions. If there is a solution, it’s probably in software.
But software is hard to create. Good software is even harder. But that’s not because you need magic wizards to write the most arcane code (most of the time) but because software is not what most people think it is: Software is not (just) the lines of programming code.
Good software flows from good requirements analysis, from understanding the real problem that is to be solved and it’s domain and organizational embedding, from understanding the needs, abilities and situation of the people using the software, it flows from thinking about good architecture that describes the structure of the whole construct often even before a line of code has been typed. It’s a bit of an exaggeration but I’m still gonna say it: The programming code is kind of an afterthought a lot of the time. The whole gestalt of the software has been described (or at least conceptualized) way way before.
But that process is very hard and messy and therefore costly. Taking the time to actually understand domain, problem and people is a lot of effort especially when knowing that when building special software for a context you will run into many social problems that you need to navigate (like: Putting function A into department B would make the most sense but department C is never gonna give that function up because of internal politics and power struggles). Many if not most problems in software development are actually social problems. Good software therefore flows from empathy and listening.
Just vibing output
As it is usual with promises of “AI” thi

• [brudgers] 仅提供了一个存档链接，没有明确表达立场或看法。

data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 一项新研究发表在《Nature Astronomy》上，由加州理工学院的Konstantin Batygin和密歇根大学的Fred C. Adams领导，揭示了木星在其早期形成阶段的特征。研究表明，木星曾经是当前大小的两倍，半径约为现有半径的两倍，体积相当于2000多个地球。此外，木星当时的磁场比现在强约50倍。研究人员通过分析木星的小卫星Amalthea和Thebe的轨道偏差得出这些结论，绕过了传统行星形成模型中的不确定性。这项研究为了解太阳系的形成提供了重要线索，并为木星及其演化过程提供了更精确的早期测量数据。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：木星的形成、演化及其大小变化的相关问题

不同观点：

• lukan对WalterBright的观点提出质疑，引用维基百科说明木星的直径在其组成和演化历史中已达最大，并询问这是否是新发现或以前假设的一部分。

The GIST
Jupiter was formerly twice its current size and had a much stronger magnetic field, study says
by Lori Dajose,
California Institute of Technology
edited by
Lisa Lock
, 																								reviewed by
Robert Egan
Editors' notes

and

peer-reviewed publication
trusted source
proofread
An illustration of Jupiter with magnetic field lines emitting from its poles. Credit: Credit: K. Batygin
Understanding Jupiter's early evolution helps illuminate the broader story of how our solar system developed its distinct structure. Jupiter's gravity, often called the "architect" of our solar system, played a critical role in shaping the orbital paths of other planets and sculpting the disk of gas and dust from which they formed.
In a new study
published
in the journal
Nature Astronomy
, Konstantin Batygin, professor of planetary science at Caltech; and Fred C. Adams, professor of physics and astronomy at the University of Michigan; provide a detailed look into Jupiter's primordial state.
Their calculations reveal that roughly 3.8 million years after the solar system's first solids formed—a key moment when the disk of material around the sun, known as the protoplanetary nebula, was dissipating—Jupiter was significantly larger and had an even more powerful magnetic field.
"Our ultimate goal is to understand where we come from, and pinning down the early phases of planet formation is essential to solving the puzzle," Batygin says. "This brings us closer to understanding how not only Jupiter but the entire solar system took shape."
Batygin and Adams approached this question by studying Jupiter's tiny moons Amalthea and Thebe, which orbit even closer to Jupiter than Io, the smallest and nearest of the planet's four large Galilean moons.
Because Amalthea and Thebe have slightly tilted orbits, Batygin and Adams analyzed these small orbital discrepancies to calculate Jupiter's original size: approximately twice its current radius, with a predicted volume that is the equivalent of over 2,000 Earths. The researchers also determined that Jupiter's magnetic field at that time was approximately 50 times stronger than it is today.
Adams highlights the remarkable imprint the past has left on today's solar system: "It's astonishing that even after 4.5 billion years, enough clues remain to let us reconstruct Jupiter's physical state at the dawn of its existence."
Importantly, these insights were achieved through independent constraints that bypass traditional uncertainties in planetary formation models—which often rely on assumptions about gas opacity, accretion rate, or the mass of the heavy element core. Instead, the team focused on the orbital dynamics of Jupiter's moons and the conservation of the planet's angular momentum—quantities that are directly measurable.
Their analysis establishes a clear snapshot of Jupiter at the moment the surrounding solar nebula evaporated, a pivotal transition point when the
building materials
for planet formation disappeared and the primordial architecture of the solar system was locked in.
The results add crucial details to existing planet formation theories, which suggest that Jupiter and other
giant planets
around other stars formed via core accretion, a process by which a rocky and icy core rapidly gathers gas.
These foundational models were developed over decades by many researchers, including Caltech's Dave Stevenson, the Marvin L. Goldberger Professor of Planetary Science, Emeritus. This new study builds upon that foundation by providing more exact measurements of Jupiter's size, spin rate, and magnetic conditions at an early, pivotal time.
Batygin emphasizes that while Jupiter's first moments remain obscured by uncertainty, the current research significantly clarifies our picture of the planet's critical developmental stages. "What we've established here is a valuable benchmark," he says. "A point from which we can more confidently reconstruct the evolution of our
solar system
."

Nature Astronomy
(2025).

data.title: A boy who came back: the near-death, and changed life, of my son Max
data.author: ljf
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者Archie Bland的儿子Max遭遇突发健康危机，险些夭折的经历。那天原本是个普通的日子，作者和家人享受着日常的平静生活。然而，Max突然停止了呼吸和心跳。作者和妻子在慌乱中进行了急救，并在医护人员到来前恢复了Max的部分生命体征。Max被紧急送往医院，最终幸存下来，但这次事件彻底改变了作者对 parenting、残疾以及生命意义的理解。文章通过生动的细节描写，展现了作者在面对儿子生死未卜时的恐惧、无助和内心的自我责备。最终，Max虽然活了下来，但他们的生活已发生了不可逆转的变化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对一篇感人故事的回应与反思，涉及残障、医疗体系和家庭照护问题

不同观点：
• [liamwire] 认为文章唤起了他童年与患有脑瘫的孩子一起成长的记忆，表示文章非常感人，让他重新思考那些早已遗忘的情感。他强调自己当时并不觉得有任何异常，显示出一种对残障的自然接受态度。

• [AStonesThrow] 对文章标题和内容预期之间的差异表示不满，原本期待一个奇迹康复的故事，但实际内容却是关于接受残障生活的现实。他还批评了医疗体系，尤其是NHS（英国国家医疗服务体系），认为其在诊断和处理婴儿猝死综合症（SIDS）等问题上存在不足。此外，他还提到社会对父母在类似情况下所承受压力的误解。

• [insane_dreamer] 称赞文章写得很好，并以自己作为残疾儿童家长的身份强调了对文章中某些诚实表述的认同。他批评了社会对残障儿童家长的压力，即要求他们公开表示不会希望孩子恢复健康，认为这种期望是不现实的。

补充讨论：
• 文章引发的对残障生活的深思，尤其是对“是否希望改变孩子状况”这一问题的讨论，反映出社会对残障的复杂态度。
• [AStonesThrow] 提到了对医疗专业人员和诊断过程的不满，特别是对“SIDS”等问题的处理，暗示了对医疗体系的不信任。
• [insane_dreamer] 提到社会对残障儿童家长的不当言论问题，并表示自己幸运地没有遇到太多这样的情况，暗示了社会支持和理解的重要性。

争议焦点：
• 文章标题是否具有误导性，导致读者预期与实际内容不符。
• 社会对残障儿童家长的期望和压力是否合理，以及如何改善对这些家庭的社会支持。
• 对医疗体系在处理残障和复杂医疗情况时的能力和态度的批评与反思。

Photograph: Lydia Goldblatt/The Guardian
View image in fullscreen
Archie Bland with his son, Max.
Photograph: Lydia Goldblatt/The Guardian
Family
The boy who came back: the near-death, and changed life, of my son Max
It was, we were told, a case of sudden infant death syndrome interrupted. What followed would transform my understanding of parenting, disability and the breadth of what makes a meaningful life
Archie Bland
Sat 24 May 2025 01.00 EDT
Share
I look back at the last day of our old life with a kind of wonder now: the million summer freedoms, the complacency of our ease.
I watched the cricket with Max on my knee. Friends came to visit, and Ruth fed Max while we talked about our new neighbourhood among piles of books and packing boxes. Max gurgled regally as I changed one of his famous nappies. I organised our phone chargers and put his birth certificate carefully in a drawer with our passports and the mortgage statement. Then I hung a picture in what would soon be his room: a print from
Maurice Sendak’s Where the Wild Things Are
, of a little boy sailing bravely across the ocean, with “Max” emblazoned on the prow of his ship. I stood back and admired it, feeling all three of us to be limitless, and wondering what would happen next.
Ruth called her mum and gave her the latest; I told one group chat I thought Ring doorbells were for dickheads, and asked another what had been happening at work during my paternity leave. I ate half a chocolate bar, then forgot about it. Finding it a week later levelled me. This melted Dairy Milk, left for me by another person entirely, a stranger from an antique land.
Then I have an in-between memory. I woke at five and stumbled to the bathroom to drink from the tap. The house was silent. Maybe the unknowable internal dominoes had already started to fall, or maybe they could still have been stopped. Maybe I could have decided to get Max up early, for no particular reason. Gina, the night nanny helping us through the move, would have thought me strange, but it would have been fine. Or if I had picked him up for a cuddle and put him straight back. Or if changing any single moment in his life or mine might have made everything different. A different bedtime. A different bed. A different house. A different dad.
Just before six, the day already too hot, the pallid dawn creeping around the blinds: Gina’s voice, bursting into our room, screaming, blurred by a dream. I don’t remember her words. She is holding Max towards us, maybe hoping we will say she is wrong and he is fine. But he has no pulse, and he is not breathing. He is limp, cold, the colour of marble.
Then I am calling 999 for the first time in my life while Gina starts CPR. I am saying our address again and again, begging the operator to start telling us what to do. I am distractingly aware that I am naked in the presence of someone I hardly know. Now Ruth takes the phone, and under the operator’s instructions we move Max from the bed to the floor. Now Ruth calls out a rhythm while I press at his little chest with my clumsy thumbs, then pause for Gina to breathe into his mouth.
There is a voice in my head. You and Gina should not be dividing this responsibility, it says. You have introduced a layer of confusion. You should have taken charge. These are the things you have to get right at the most important moment of your life. This is happening. You are his father. This is
your
job. These will always be the things that you did. You are failing, and now your son is dead. “Please, please,” I say, sobbing as I count. All three of us are saying it. “Please, Max, please.”
A police car is nearby, and they arrive a few minutes after six. Ruth runs down to let them in, I think. We stagger dumbly back, and let someone lead us out of the room.
We are told to ride with him in the back of the ambulance because there is every chance he will not survive the journey
Max is still on the floor when the paramedics arrive a few minutes later, their notes tell me, but the police have done an excellent job with a defibrillator. The paramedics attach pads which adjust the shock to his size. He has no pulse. They push a tube down his throat to stop his tongue from blocking his airway. Then they put a bag over his nose and mouth which forces air into his lungs. Max is gasping once or twice a minute. But his heart starts beating again.
At six minutes to seven, we leave for the hospital. At some point I must have found some clothes.
I sit in the front of the ambulance and say thank you to the driver. When we get there, a paramedic tells us Max has opened his eyes. I cannot calibrate what this means. Perhaps it will be a near miss, a story we will tell.
Max is rushed past us into A&E. I haven’t really seen him in an hour, just the cloud of people and equipment that attends him. Ruth, Gina and I are taken to a cramped waiting room, full of stacked chairs. I stare at the ceiling. An insect crawls along a fluorescen

• [AStonesThrow] 对文章标题和内容预期之间的差异表示不满，原本期待一个奇迹康复的故事，但实际内容却是关于接受残障生活的现实。他还批评了医疗体系，尤其是NHS（英国国家医疗服务体系），认为其在诊断和处理婴儿猝死综合症（SIDS）等问题上存在不足。此外，他还提到社会对父母在类似情况下所承受压力的误解。

• [insane_dreamer] 称赞文章写得很好，并以自己作为残疾儿童家长的身份强调了对文章中某些诚实表述的认同。他批评了社会对残障儿童家长的压力，即要求他们公开表示不会希望孩子恢复健康，认为这种期望是不现实的。

补充讨论：
• 文章引发的对残障生活的深思，尤其是对“是否希望改变孩子状况”这一问题的讨论，反映出社会对残障的复杂态度。
• [AStonesThrow] 提到了对医疗专业人员和诊断过程的不满，特别是对“SIDS”等问题的处理，暗示了对医疗体系的不信任。
• [insane_dreamer] 提到社会对残障儿童家长的不当言论问题，并表示自己幸运地没有遇到太多这样的情况，暗示了社会支持和理解的重要性。

争议焦点：
• 文章标题是否具有误导性，导致读者预期与实际内容不符。

data.title: Autopsy of an LHC Beam Dump
data.author: voxadam
data.article_summary: 2022年，CERN首次对大型强子对撞机（LHC）的放射性束流吸收器进行了“解剖”分析，以了解材料在高能束流影响下的行为。由于运行十年后，LHC的两个外部束流吸收器出现退化迹象（如氮泄漏），被替换下来。为查明泄漏原因，进行了内窥镜检查，发现吸收器内的挤压石墨圆盘出现裂缝。为获取更多信息并为LHC及高亮度LHC（HL-LHC）设计新备用吸收器，必须对吸收器进行“解剖”。由于其放射性，切割其双相不锈钢合金外壳极具挑战。最终，CERN团队开发了远程切割技术，成功完成解剖。结果显示，低密度和高密度石墨状况良好，但挤压石墨不适合用于新备用吸收器设计。进一步的材料研究正在进行中，以确认结果并测试HL-LHC的新材料。现有吸收器的改造应能提高其在第三次运行中的耐受性。

主要讨论点：围绕CERN（欧洲核子研究中心）相关技术的讨论，包括放射性、实验设备以及工程美学。

不同观点：
• **exabrial** 关注放射性和材料转变：  
  - 提问钢壳和石墨哪一个会变得具有放射性。  
  - 关心在实验过程中发生的材料转变（transmutation）类型。

• **andrewrn** 分享个人经历，强调参与但理解有限：  
  - 描述了在本科期间参与LHC（大型强子对撞机） beauty项目探测器组装的经历。  
  - 表示自己当时仅是实验室助理，并没有完全理解背后的物理学原理，但依然觉得参与其中很酷。

• **RetroTeche** 从视觉角度评论，表达对工程技术的赞赏：  
  - 指出CERN内部的照片常常与科幻主题的3A游戏难以区分。  
  - 强调这是尖端工程的体现，表现出对工程美学的欣赏。

• **tux3** 提到技术故障，关注设备维护：  
  - 提到在阅读相关内容时，CERN的束流倾倒（beam dumps）设备刚好在使用。  
  - 指出故障与12区的淬火保护（quench protection）有关，并表示希望磁体没有受损。

补充讨论：
- 评论中涉及到放射性材料科学、个人参与大型科研项目的感受、工程设备的美学价值以及技术故障的实际操作问题，展示了多角度的讨论。

français
Autopsy of an LHC beam dump
For the first time at CERN, an autopsy has been carried out on a radioactive beam dump. Inspection of the inner workings of the device helped the teams to find out more about how materials behave under the impact of high-energy beams
8 June, 2022
|
By
Anaïs Schaeffer
The beam dump is moved into the radiation airlock installation specially constructed for the autopsy.
(Image: CERN)
During LS2, the LHC’s two external beam dumps were removed from the tunnel and replaced with spare ones. After ten years of operation, they were showing signs of degradation, notably nitrogen leaks. Before being installed, the spare dumps were modified and upgraded to prevent the same problems from occurring during Run 3 (see
this
Bulletin
article
published in 2020).
To find out more about the cause of the nitrogen leaks, an endoscopy was carried out in July 2020. It revealed unexpected cracks in the beam dump’s two extruded graphite discs (see box). An action plan was drawn up by the SY-STI (Sources, Targets and Interactions) group as more information was needed with Run 3 on the horizon, especially with a view to designing new spare beam dumps for the LHC and, beyond that, beam dumps for the HL-LHC. To access the dump’s three main components – high-density, low-density and extruded graphite (see below) – there was only one possible solution: perform an “autopsy” on one of the dumps. Given its radioactivity levels, this was easier said than done.
“To reach the heart of the beam dump, we needed to be able to open it…,” says project leader Ana-Paula Bernardes. “But its duplex-stainless-steel-alloy housing was extremely difficult to cut. The first attempt, in January 2021, under a framework contract, was unsuccessful: it was impossible to cut through it manually without exceeding the radiation dose limits. We considered outsourcing the job to a specialised external company with the right equipment for the task, but the costs and time frames were incompatible with the project.”
Top: Longitudinal test cut with the circular saw, performed by the SY-STI group. Solution chosen for the cutting of the radioactive dump. Middle: Positioning of the automated, rail-mounted circular saw for the first radial cut, performed by the SY-STI group. Bottom: The first longitudinal cut.
(Images: CERN)
Thanks to the expertise and versatility of CERN’s teams, a solution was eventually found in house: the SY-STI and BE-CEM (Controls, Electronics and Mechatronics) groups worked together to develop two techniques that would allow the dump’s housing to be cut remotely. The first involved an automated circular saw mounted on a rail, and the second a robot arm equipped with a cutter.
Longitudinal test cut with the robot arm, performed by the BE-CEM group. (Image: CERN)
Several trial runs were carried out on a mock-up in order to “choreograph” the operation and thus limit, as far as possible, the time spent in close proximity to the dump. The circular saw was ultimately used to make five cuts, in a radiation airlock installation created specially for the job: two radial cuts to separate the low-density graphite block and three longitudinal cuts to remove the stainless-steel-alloy housing.
The highly radioactive stainless-steel-alloy housing is removed by the EN-HE (Handling Engineering) group to allow access to the low-density graphite.(Image: CERN)
“As the endoscopy had already shown, both extruded graphite discs were cracked. Against all expectations, the low-density graphite was generally in good condition, as were the high-density-graphite blocks,” says Ana-Paula Bernardes.
The upstream extruded graphite disc (the first to be hit by the beam) is cracked. (Image: CERN)
“It was important to check the condition of the various components of the dump and establish how resistant they were, for various reasons,” explains Marco Calviani, leader of the Targets, Collimators and Dumps (STI-TCD) section in the SY department. “First of all, we needed to be sure that the dumps currently installed in the LHC – which are built from the same components as the autopsied dump – would withstand the energy levels of Run 3; next, we wanted to know what strategy to adopt for the two new spare dumps, which we need to design and manufacture by 2023, and especially for the dumps for the future HL-LHC.”
The results of the autopsy validated the use of low-density and high-density graphite for Run 3, but ruled out the use of extruded graphite for the design of the spare dumps. Other studies are under way at the HiRadMat facility (see the corresponding article entitled
“What will the future LHC beam dumps be made of?”
) to confirm these results and to test new materials, notably for the HL-LHC beam dumps.   - 关心在实验过程中发生的材料转变（transmutation）类型。

• **andrewrn** 分享个人经历，强调参与但理解有限：  
  - 描述了在本科期间参与LHC（大型强子对撞机） beauty项目探测器组装的经历。  
  - 表示自己当时仅是实验室助理，并没有完全理解背后的物理学原理，但依然觉得参与其中很酷。

• **RetroTeche** 从视觉角度评论，表达对工程技术的赞赏：  
  - 指出CERN内部的照片常常与科幻主题的3A游戏难以区分。  
  - 强调这是尖端工程的体现，表现出对工程美学的欣赏。

• **tux3** 提到技术故障，关注设备维护：  
  - 提到在阅读相关内容时，CERN的束流倾倒（beam dumps）设备刚好在使用。  
  - 指出故障与12区的淬火保护（quench protection）有关，并表示希望磁体没有受损。

补充讨论：
- 评论中涉及到放射性材料科学、个人参与大型科研项目的感受、工程设备的美学价值以及技术故障的实际操作问题，展示了多角度的讨论。
- 争议焦点并不明显，但**exabrial**对材料放射性的具体细节有疑问，其他评论者没有直接回应这一技术问题。

data.title: Silly job interview questions in Haskell
data.author: behnamoh
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了几个常见的面试问题在Haskell中的实现方法。首先讨论了回文判断函数`isPalindrome`，其核心逻辑非常直观，即比较字符串与其反转是否相同。接着演示了经典的Fizz Buzz问题，通过定义辅助函数`fizzle`来处理不同的条件判断，并使用高阶函数`for_`实现循环输出。然后分析了一个较少见的问题，即找出列表中三个数之和等于指定值的所有组合。文章展示了如何通过递归实现组合生成，并利用过滤器获取符合条件的组合。总体展示了Haskell函数式编程的简洁性和强大表达能力。
