data.title: When good pseudorandom numbers go bad
data.author: chewxy
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了在实际计算机中进行矩阵特征值分解时可能出现的误差问题，引用了Wilkinson（1965）的研究。即使对于具有重复实特征值的实不对称矩阵，计算结果也可能出现复共轭特征值对。文章还描述了作者同事在使用R语言进行多变量正态分布模拟时遇到的不可重现性问题，尽管使用了`set.seed()`来控制随机数生成器状态，但在不同机器上仍得到不同的随机数结果。作者最终发现问题根源在于浮点运算的特性，这导致计算机行为与预期不符。这一问题并非来自`set.seed()`或`MASS::mvrnorm()`函数本身，而是浮点运算的固有缺陷。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在计算机科学中，关于随机函数和哈希函数的使用及其可再现性的问题

不同观点：
• somat认为，人们常常误将随机函数当作哈希函数使用，导致出现问题。他指出，随机函数在不同版本和系统之间没有硬性规范，结果不可预测，而哈希函数则是确定性的。随机函数本质上是非确定性的，不应该期待其具有可再现性。

• AlotOfReading持不同观点，认为大多数人实际上关心的是可再现性，而不是数值稳定性和正确性。他指出，在现代硬件上，通过遵循一些基本原则（如同样的输入、同样的操作顺序、避免特殊函数等），可以实现实际的可再现性，且性能成本很低。然而，由于工具链和用户知识的问题，这种可再现性并未得到优先考虑。

补充讨论：
• mjcohen提到自己过去的经验，表明在不同硬件和设置下，算法的性能可能会有显著差异（如VAX Fortran中下标检查增加30%的运行时间），但未直接涉及主要讨论点。

• coolcase对讨论内容不太理解，询问是否涉及 race condition、硬件差异或浮点运算的随机性，这反映了部分读者对讨论技术细节的困惑。

• jam0wal以简明的语言指出，如果需要恒定输出，直接使用常量数组即可，而不应将偏见强加于随机函数的解释上。

争议焦点：
主要争议在于随机函数和哈希函数的使用及其可再现性。somat强调随机函数的不可预测性，而AlotOfReading则认为在一定条件下，现代硬件可以实现可再现性。

44027229.article_content:
Computing the eigendecomposition of a matrix is subject to errors on a real-world computer: the definitive analysis is Wilkinson (1965). All you can hope for is a solution to a problem suitably close to x. So even though a real asymmetric x may have an algebraic solution with repeated real eigenvalues, the computed solution may be of a similar matrix with complex conjugate pairs of eigenvalues.
–
help("eigen")
A few weeks ago, in the beforetimes when I’d not personally had the soul-crushingly unpleasant experience of being infected with that covid-19 thing,
1
some colleagues
2
approached me to talk about a reproducibility issue they’d been having with some R code. They’d been running simulations that rely on generating samples from a multivariate normal distribution, and despite doing the prudent thing and using
set.seed()
to control the state of the random number generator (RNG), the results were not computationally reproducible. The same code, executed on different machines, would produce different random numbers. The numbers weren’t “just a little bit different” in the way that we’ve all wearily learned to expect when you try to force computers to do mathematics. They wer painfully, brutally, catastrophically, irreproducible different. Somewhere, somehow, something broke.
3
4
That’s not supposed to happen…
Somehow, “Palpatine” returned. Palpatine was floating point errors all along.
… and to be fair, in most situations it
doesn’t
happen. Most computations are reproducible, and even random number generation does what it’s supposed to do as long as you’re careful with the seed. Or, to put it more plainly, the
set.seed()
method for controlling the results of your computations in R works just fine. At the risk of being tiresome, here’s a “random” permutation of the letters of the English alphabet that we obtain in R after the seed is fixed:
set.seed
(
1
L)
sample
(letters)
[1] "y" "d" "g" "a" "b" "k" "n" "r" "w" "j" "f" "t" "q" "x" "i" "e" "u" "l"
[19] "s" "p" "o" "m" "v" "z" "c" "h"
Here is
THE SAME BLOODY PERMUTATION
of those letters, produced a second time because the author is bored and she wants you to understand that this is a quarto document so everything that you see here is being done in an actual R session and she is not making it up:
set.seed
(
1
L)
sample
(letters)
[1] "y" "d" "g" "a" "b" "k" "n" "r" "w" "j" "f" "t" "q" "x" "i" "e" "u" "l"
[19] "s" "p" "o" "m" "v" "z" "c" "h"
Because the original code and the replication code both use
set.seed(1)
before calling
sample()
to shuffle the letters of the alphabet into a random order, we get the
same
random permutation in both cases. And although I’m executing this code twice on the same machine, there’s no reason to expect that it would make a difference if I ran the original code on my ubuntu laptop running R 4.4.3 or on a window machine running R 4.3.1. It “should” be the same result either way. I mean… that’s the whole purpose of
set.seed()
. It’s “supposed” to make your code reproducible, even though you are doing “random” things with that code. Right?
Well. It might. If you’re lucky.
That’s not what my colleagues experienced with their code when generating multivariate random normal samples. In their case, different machines produced different random samples even though the code used
set.seed()
to (ostensibly) prevent that from happening. Quite reasonably, their first thought was “
WHAT THE FUCK IS THIS???
”.
Having encountered the problem, their second thought was that it was their fault:
they
must have done something wrong with their code that caused the simulations to break. It wasn’t that. Their code was fine. Their third thought was that something was wrong with R itself, or more precisely with
MASS::mvrnorm()
, since this is the function that was causing all the difficulty. They couldn’t see anything wrong with the function though, so they asked me to look into it.
My first thought, when they oh-so-innocently dropped a nuclear weapon on my desk, was that MASS could not possibly be the problem. I mean, not really. It’s a very carefully tested package, it is very widely used, it’s fine. Right? Though… actually, now that I think of it
MASS::mvrnorm()
is a very old function, and it makes some assumptions about what happens at a lower level that might not be right. So… maybe it is the problem??? I don’t really know…
Look, it’s complicated okay?
So let me get back to you on that because when you track down far enough, the root cause of the problem my colleagues ran into wasn’t really the MASS package. The actual problem turned out to be the inconvenient fact that
floating point arithmetic
does not behave like real arithmetic, and that in turn has the teeeeensy tiny side effect that computers very often don’t do what people expect them to do.
Le sigh.
I should have known. In hindsight it was so obviously going to be floating point issues
5
that I shouldn’t have spent hours/days/weeks looking into it. As I said on Mastodon at the time:
In future, w

data.title: Adventures in Symbolic Algebra with Model Context Protocol
data.author: freediver
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了作者使用MCP协议将语言模型（LLM）与符号计算机代数系统结合的实验。LLM擅长理解自然语言描述的数学问题，但在解决这些问题上表现不佳，而计算机代数系统则擅长符号运算。通过MCP协议，可以将两者的优势结合，LLM负责理解和规划，代数系统负责精确计算。作者使用GitHub上的开源代码演示了这一过程，尽管代码尚不成熟。MCP协议类似于AI工具的标准化接口，允许语言模型调用外部工具，但存在一定安全风险。调试MCP服务器颇具挑战，因其非确定性导致调试复杂。最终，作者通过简单示例展示了该方法的有效性，如让LLM分解大整数，结果显示LLM常给出错误答案，而代数系统则能准确完成任务。

主要讨论点：围绕MCP（可能指某种多功能计算平台或工具）及其与LLM（大型语言模型）和符号AI结合的讨论，包括实际应用、技术挑战、可扩展性问题以及与现有工具的比较。

不同观点：
• crystal_revenge认为，Stephen对MCP工具的实验兴趣和适度的怀疑态度值得赞赏，但当前领域被过度炒作和极端怀疑所主导，这两种倾向都不利于实际问题的解决。

44062130.article_content:
Adventures in Symbolic Algebra with Model Context Protocol
I spent last weekend playing with this new
MCP protocol
all the kids are talking about, using it to make language models talk to symbolic computer algebra systems. The idea was simple: LLMs are great at understanding natural language math problems but terrible at actually solving them, while computer algebra systems excel at symbolic manipulation but have arcane interfaces. By connecting them through MCP, we can get the best of both worlds. The code is still early and rough around the edges, but I've put the source up on Github if anyone wants to experiment with it.
Github Source Code
(
git clone https://github.com/sdiehl/sympy-mcp.git
)
MCP, if you're not familiar, is Anthropic's answer to the question: "How do we get an LLM to actually DO things instead of just TALK about doing them?" It's essentially the
cgi-bin
of AI (I'm probably dating myself with that reference). It's a protocol that allows language models to call external tools through a server that exposes the functions as a REST API. The core idea of MCP is to standardize the way language models call external tools, instead of writing custom connectors for each AI model and each tool, you implement the protocol once on each side. It's the USB-C of AI tooling, if USB-C were still in its awkward adolescent phase.
Notably, the MCP server runs locally on your machine, letting the language model invoke arbitrary code and commands by using one of the LLM desktop clients to call out to the local server. This is probably a bad idea in general and as dangerous and reckless as you might think, so there's a definite security concern here ... be warned. But let's not let a potential rootkit get in the way of a fun weekend experiment.
My particular itch stemmed from watching Claude (and its cousins like o4-mini-high and DeepSeek-R1) really struggle with tensor calculus. If you've ever asked an LLM to perform complex symbolic manipulation, you know the drill: confident answers, beautiful LaTeX formatting, and results that would make your math professor weep bitter tears. These models, despite their impressive linguistic capabilities, are absolute disasters when it comes to keeping track of indices in tensor expressions or manipulating complicated algebraic forms. The expressions involved in even moderate general relativity problems are HUGE, with hundreds of terms and complex
index gymnastics
.
But we already have specialized tools that excel at this! Computer algebra systems like Mathematica, Sympy, xAct, Cadabra were built specifically for this purpose. So the obvious solution presented itself: let's expose these tools to the LLM through MCP and let each system do what it does best. The LLM handles the natural language understanding and planning, while the symbolic algebra system performs the actual mathematical manipulations with perfect precision.
Working with the MCP ecosystem is like visiting a frontier town in the Wild West. The documentation exists in the form of scattered campfire stories, the implementations have a distinctly "I wrote this at a 3 AM hackathon" vibe, and everything is strangely Node-heavy. This Node fixation likely stems from most MCP tools being designed to call REST services for cloud applications. Then there's the peculiar ecosystem of suspiciously self-referential products from companies that just happen to sell AI coding assistants. There's definitely a faint whiff of opportunism in the air.
Debugging an MCP server is a crazy exercise. You're essentially working with a stochastic black box that communicates through a complex web of JSON schemas attached to docstring annotations. When something goes wrong, good luck figuring out if it's your server, the client, the LLM's interpretation, or just the model having a laugh at your expense. The non-deterministic nature of the whole setup means that something can work perfectly five times in a row and then spontaneously fail on the sixth attempt because the random number seed on the inference server is different, the prompt vibes are off, or for reasons completely shrouded in the mists of the digital occult. Welcome to the fun future of software.
However, once you've made the ritual animal sacrifice to appease the non-determinism gods (I find that sacrificing a rubber duck while chanting
"Ph'nglui mglw'nafh Roko's Basilisk R'lyeh wgah'nagl fhtagn, O Great Transformer of the Deep, may thy hallucinations be few and thy completions true"
works best), you'll find the basic implementation is refreshingly straightforward, similar to FastAPI if FastAPI were designing its endpoints for a language model. Here's a simple example that highlights why this approach matters: Ask any LLM to factor a large integer, and watch it confidently fabricate entirely wrong answers. By design, transformers can't perform the arbitrary computation required for integer factorization. They've merely memorized some factorizations from the internet (and even th

data.title: Don't "buy" e-books from Oxford University Press
data.author: pvdebbe
data.article_summary: 作者在文章中分享了购买一本电子书的糟糕经历。起初，作者选择购买牛津大学出版社的电子书《Music Copyright, Creativity, and Culture》，以为能够下载并自由使用。然而，购买后发现无法下载，只能通过VitalSource的在线平台或其专有应用程序访问，且内容受DRM保护，无法打印或复制。作者试图通过打印功能获取PDF版本，结果生成的文件质量极差，满是水印且文字无法选择和搜索。作者对此体验感到不满，表示今后不会从这些平台购买任何电子书，并呼吁大家团结抗议此类行为，而不是互相孤立。最终，作者通过本地书店购买了纸质书，真正拥有了可自由阅读的书籍。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：数字版权管理（DRM）和消费者选择之间的争议，特别是在电子书购买中的应用。

不同观点：
• thephyber：认为消费者应选择实体书，以抵制反消费者的数字发行公司，并指出实体书仅比租赁的数字版本贵一美元。同时建议如果退货政策无效，可以通过信用卡公司寻求帮助。

• diggan：指出在想要合法获取无DRM电子书时面临的困境，特别是对于特定出版社（如Oxford University Press）的书籍。质疑在仅有的购买选项都不理想时，消费者的选择，并提到避免购买或盗版是无奈的应对方式。

• ndsipa_pomu：认为盗版是应对消费者敌对政策的方法，并指出过度使用DRM会促使更多人考虑盗版。

• jmclnx：坚决避免使用电子书，除非它们是无DRM的标准PDF文件，能够在任何操作系统上查看，否则偏好实体书。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于消费者在面对带有DRM限制的数字内容时，缺乏合理的选择和灵活性。
• 讨论中提到了盗版问题，部分评论者认为这是消费者对抗DRM限制的现实回应，但也有对这一做法的伦理和法律考量。
• 消费者对电子书和实体书的价格、便利性及所有权的不同看法也构成了讨论的一部分。

Last month I watched the book talk

Alliance:

Copyright, Creativity, and Culture - Jennifer Jenkins
Looking to get a copy of the book, I found the book’s page on the
publisher’s website, Oxford University Press.  Seeing it available as
an e-book, I opted to go with that as a more eco-friendly option and
to save some physical space.  I worked my way through the checkout and
payment steps, under the impression that I would be purchasing a copy
of the book that I could download and do with as I wished.  The use
of the words “buy” and “purchase” throughout the book page on the
publisher’s website certainly did not suggest otherwise.
In hindsight, there were red flags I failed to notice at the time,
such as confusing and seemingly redundant, if not contradictory,
information on the book page:
“Downloaded copy on your device does not expire.”
Um, okay?  I’d sure hope and expect as much about any file I download.
“Includes 4 years of Bookshelf Online.”
Whatever — as long as I could download, store, and use the book
offline I’d be happy.
It’s only upon hovering the small and generic, if not misleading,
“E-book purchasing help” link that one would be presented with this
vaguely informative eyebrow-raising sentence:
E-book purchase
E-books are granted under the terms of a single-user,
non-transferable license, and may be accessed online from any
location.
“E-books are granted” (??) is news to me.  I thought I would have
rightful access to something I bought and paid for, rather than being
“granted” (read “allowed”) access to it by and through some overlord.
Oh but of course, we live in a time where vendors get to redefine
well-established words like “purchase” and “buy” on page N of their
terms and conditions.
I obviously did not see that “E-book purchasing help” before giving
Oxford University Press my money: being a tech-savvy person, I didn’t
think I needed any help “purchasing” an e-book.
Everything became clear shortly after I completed the “purchase” and
was redirected to VitalSource to access the book: the VitalSource
“Bookshelf” user interface offered no way to download a copy of the
book I thought I bought and paid for.  It is instead a glorified pile
of proprietary JavaScript DRM (
Digital Restrictions Management
)
that wraps around the underlying representation of the book in
VitalSource’s possession.  The only other option for accessing the
book would be through VitalSource’s proprietary application available
only for certain versions of certain proprietary operating systems.
At this point, the only method I could think of to try and obtain a
copy of the book that I could read without subjecting myself to the
shackles of DRM or proprietary software was trying to
print
the
book to PDF.  Given that VitalSource’s DRM interface is a proprietary
wrapper around VitalSource’s likely ePub-based underlying
representation (guessing from the presence of
epubcfi
in the URL of
their book renderer page), the book pages are not exposed all at once,
practically forcing one to use the interface’s Print function to get
all the pages in one go.  After waiting what felt like an eternity
for the website to prepare a printable version of the book, I was
presented with this abomination (click image for sample in original
PDF form):
That is a sample of the output generated by the interface’s Print
function: an utterly useless, inferior copy of the book that has giant
watermarks on
every single page
, with the only selectable text in
the whole book being the repugnant threat at the top of each page —
the actual body text of the book is converted to low-resolution,
blurry images, and is therefore neither selectable nor searchable.
Going forward, I will
NEVER
“purchase” anything from Oxford
University Press (and most definitely not from VitalSource), so long
as they have no problem “selling” [access to] DRM-infested copies of
books with no way to download a usable copy of what I paid for.
The key takeaway for me from this whole experience is that due to the
sad and sorry status quo of our current times, this kind of insulting
(mal)treatment of users is all but common, and really can happen to
any one of us.  Therefore it is all the more important for us to band
together in protest of this, rather than dividing and isolating
ourselves through misguided better-than-thou sentiments toward
each other.
For Music Copyright, Creativity, and Culture, I ordered and a few days
later received a paper copy from the local bookstore.  It’s a copy
I truly own, and can read whenever, wherever, and however I please.
Take care, and so long for now.

(spoiler: you can’t)

data.author: ayoisaiah
data.article_summary: F2是一个跨平台的命令行工具，用于快速、安全地批量重命名文件和目录，采用Go语言编写。它具有以下特点：默认进行模拟运行（Dry Run），可在执行前预览更改；支持使用文件属性如图片的EXIF数据或音频的ID3标签进行重命名；提供全面的重命名选项，包括简单字符串替换和复杂正则表达式；注重安全性，通过严格检查确保无冲突和错误；自动解决检测到的冲突；性能高，能快速处理大量文件；具备撤销功能，可轻松纠正错误。F2文档详尽，提供实际示例帮助用户上手。可通过Go安装或下载预编译二进制文件进行安装。项目采用MIT许可证。

不同观点：
• 支持vidir工具：评论[037]推荐使用Unix风格的vidir工具，认为它可以通过文本编辑器批量编辑文件名，且支持管道和文件路径的修改，非常灵活。
• 对F2工具的名称表示赞赏：评论[bsnnkv]对F2工具的名称选择表示赞赏，认为其名称唤起了怀旧感及对UX设计历史的思考。
• 推荐Double Commander的Multi Rename Tool：评论[majkinetor]提到Double Commander中的Multi Rename Tool，认为其功能接近Total Commander，并支持插件扩展。
• 强调产品UX设计的重要性：评论[nine_k]认为F2工具在UX设计上表现出色，尤其是默认的dry-run模式、使用EXIF元数据以及支持撤销操作等功能。
• 建议增加文件名样本匹配功能：评论[sandreas]希望F2工具增加一个功能，能够自动识别文件名模式并批量应用重命名规则，提到曾有类似的dotnet工具利用机器学习实现此功能。
• 对CLI设计和EXIF功能的赞赏：评论[simonw]对F2工具的CLI设计表示高度赞赏，尤其是利用EXIF信息组织图片库的功能。
• 结合Exiftool使用：评论[sorenjan]建议结合Exiftool的地理位置功能，先为照片添加城市和国家信息，再进行重命名。
• 指出文档中的小错误并提出改进建议：评论[j1elo]指出F2文档中的一个小错误，并建议增加更灵活的"--replace-range"选项。
• 表示工具非常实用：评论[devrandoom]认为F2工具非常实用，并表示会将其加入常用工具箱。
• 认为F2工具比Exiftool更灵活：评论[otterpro]认为F2工具在照片重命名方面比Exiftool更灵活。
• 对F2工具的长期使用体验表示感谢：评论[Hasnep]表示长期使用F2工具，并认为其节省了大量时间。
• 提到Windows下的PowerToys工具：评论[batrat]在Windows下使用PowerToys的Power Rename功能，认为对于非重度用户足够使用。
• 强调撤销功能的重要性：评论[hoppp]认为F2工具的撤销功能非常实用，解决了文件重命名脚本出错的问题。
• 建议增加实时预览功能：评论[porridgeraisin]认为F2工具的变量功能较为复杂，建议增加类似"up"模式的实时预览功能。

补充讨论：
• 评论中多次提到F2工具的UX设计和功能性，尤其是默认的dry-run模式、EXIF元数据支持和撤销功能，这些都被认为是其优势所在。
• 多个评论中提到了其他工具的比较，如vidir、Double Commander和Exiftool，这些工具各有优劣，用户选择依赖于具体需求和使用习惯。
• 有用户对F2工具的变量功能和复杂操作提出简化和改进建议，如增加实时预览和文件名样本匹配功能，以提升用户体验。

F2 - Command-Line Batch Renaming
F2
is a cross-platform command-line tool for batch renaming files and
directories
quickly
and
safely
. Written in Go!
What does F2 do differently?
Compared to other renaming tools, F2 offers several key advantages:
Dry Run by Default
: It defaults to a dry run so that you can review the
renaming changes before proceeding.
Variable Support
: F2 allows you to use file attributes, such as EXIF data
for images or ID3 tags for audio files, to give you maximum flexibility in
renaming.
Comprehensive Options
: Whether it's simple string replacements or complex
regular expressions, F2 provides a full range of renaming capabilities.
Safety First
: It prioritizes accuracy by ensuring every renaming operation
is conflict-free and error-proof through rigorous checks.
Conflict Resolution
: Each renaming operation is validated before execution
and detected conflicts can be automatically resolved.
High Performance
: F2 is extremely fast and efficient, even when renaming
thousands of files at once.
Undo Functionality
: Any renaming operation can be easily undone to allow
the easy correction of mistakes.
Extensive Documentation
: F2 is well-documented with clear, practical
examples to help you make the most of its features without confusion.
⚡ Installation
If you're a Go developer, F2 can be installed with
go install
(requires v1.23
or later):
go install github.com/ayoisaiah/f2/v2/cmd/f2@latest
Other installation methods are
documented here
or check
out the
releases page
to download a
pre-compiled binary for your operating system.

Trellis helps healthcare providers treat more patients, faster—while eliminating pre-service paperwork.

Trellis is a spinout from Stanford AI lab and is backed by leading investors including YC, General Catalyst, Telesoft partners, and executives at Google and Salesforce.

Be at the forefront of what's possible in AI and Healthcare data.
Work on the most important problem of our time—with direct, measurable impact.
You will work closely with the F500 customers and the founding team. You will get to wear multiple hats from sales and marketing to recruiting.
Extreme ownership: you will own key part of Trellis business operations and have the opportunities to start new initiatives.
Be a part of a world-class team (e.g., team members have previously won the international physics olympiad, published economics research, were a founding engineer at Unicorn Startup, and taught AI classes to hundreds of Stanford graduate students).

Qualify and reach out to leads based on their potential for partnership and collaboration with Trellis
Utilize modern GTM tools like Clay, Apollo and Hubspot to maintain organization and optimize the health of the sales funnel, ensuring timely follow-ups, accurate tracking, and effective prioritization of leads.
🎯 What we're looking for
Previous experience in sales role.
A proactive mindset, with the ability to take ownership of tasks and seek opportunities for process improvement
Strong verbal and written communication skills
Comfortable with ambiguity, context-switching, and operating in a fast paced environment.
You care about the details and hold yourself to the highest standard of work product
Ability to work independently, prioritize tasks, and manage time effectively to achieve goals

Reduce time to treatment by over 90%

Leverage structured data to enhance drug program performance and clinical decision-making

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI的影响及其哲学、实践和社会问题

不同观点：
• vunderba认为，AI生成的关于纽约市的描述显得自命不凡且空洞，并引用《Berserk》作者的一段话来说明人类对城市的感受表达得更好。
• 13years指出，AI不是不可避免的命运，而是一个唤醒人们的机会，但社会通常只有在事物崩溃后才会觉醒。他们还提到内容农场和噪音对知识库的冲击。
• keiferski认为，AI工具本质上只是工具集，其聊天界面可能引发了一些不必要的不安，但其核心只是帮助生成输出的工具，而非人类替代品。
• jwalton提到，ChatGPT的示例已经被房地产博客剽窃，质疑AI生成内容的原创性和使用场景。
• Garlef欣赏文章提供的AI视角，认为其避免了常见的经济角度讨论，并从meta层面反思AI，避免了过度关注经济影响。
• myaccountonhn担心AI的实际问题，如权力集中、假新闻、AI色情、数据标注中的廉价劳动力剥削等，认为哲学讨论可能是转移注意力的红鲱鱼。
• roxolotl对人们愿意将工作和自我 surrender 给生成型AI感到沮丧。
• bombdailer怀疑文章被AI修改过，认为过度使用AI可能会让内容失去生命力。
• TimorousBestie认为文章引用的海德格尔观点没有提供明确的行动呼吁，并对其适用性表示怀疑。
• pglevy引用海德格尔的《纪念演讲》来回应文章，强调对技术变革的准备不足是真正的问题。
• djoldman认为大多数人不太关心AI的哲学影响，而是试图适应。同时，LLM挑战了人类独特性的假设，使一些人感到不安。
• dtagames称赞文章是关于AI的最佳哲学作品之一。
• throwawaymaths质疑LLM生成的内容是否完全缺乏生活体验，还是源于其所喂养的集体经验。
• niemandhier指出，根据海德格尔的哲学，LLM无法与物理世界互动，因此对其“在世界中存在”的概念构成挑战。
• poopiokaka简单地认为文章明显是由AI写的，暗示对内容真实性的怀疑。

补充讨论：
• AI生成内容的原创性和人类创作的独特性是争议的焦点。
• 对AI工具的实际应用问题（如假新闻和廉价劳动力剥削）与哲学讨论之间的平衡是另一个讨论要点。
• 海德格尔的技术哲学被多次引用，以反思AI对社会和个人的深远影响。
• 一些人认为AI的聊天界面引发了不必要的不安，而另一些人则认为这是对工具本质的不理解。

data.title: Far – Sublime Inspired Find and Replace
data.author: weinzierl
data.article_summary: 该仓库包含一个名为 "Find And Replace" (far) 的命令行工具的代码，它可以快速、灵活地在文件和文件夹中搜索和替换文本。主要功能包括：搜索文本、快速替换文本、针对特定文件或目录操作、支持干运行（即将推出）以及智能大小写处理。工具灵感来源于Sublime Text的查找与替换功能。安装需通过git克隆并使用Cargo构建，支持指定文本和目标路径进行操作。该项目基于Apache-2.0许可证，欢迎提交改进建议和功能请求。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对不同工具或方法进行比较和讨论，重点在于代码中的查找与替换功能及其优势。

不同观点：
• [abcd_f] 提到另一个具有较长历史的工具 "Far Manager"，并提供了相关链接供参考。
• [mattpavelle] 对新工具与[RPL]进行比较，质疑新工具的优势，尤其是对已经习惯使用RPL的用户。
• [SubiculumCode] 希望有更多背景信息，特别是与Sublime中的查找替换功能以及sed进行比较，以突出新工具的独特性。
• [ilyagr] 提供了另外两个未被提及的工具，分别是sad和sd，为讨论引入了其他选择。
• [dima55] 对使用Perl命令行进行查找替换的方法与新工具进行比较，质疑新工具的优越性。
• [cssinate] 关注文档中的拼写错误，指出README中可能存在的错误标志`--tartget`，并怀疑实际应为`--target`。
• [llimllib] 分享了自己使用fastmod的经验，并对其表示赞赏，提供了一个Facebook孵化项目的链接。
• [iwontberude] 以幽默的方式表达了对工具命名方式的看法，没有深入技术讨论。
• [babuloseo] 仅提到"RUST"，未做详细说明或比较，可能只是表明对该语言的关注。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于新工具在查找和替换功能上是否比其他现有工具（如RPL、sed、Perl等）更具优势。
• 用户对工具的背景信息和使用场景有较多需求，希望通过比较和具体示例了解新工具的独特价值。
• 文档的准确性和拼写错误也被用户关注，表明用户在使用新工具时对文档质量有一定要求。
• 部分用户分享了自己使用的工具和经验，为讨论引入了更多选项和视角。

stands for
Find And Replace
— a fast, flexible command-line tool to search and replace text across files and folders.
Features
🔍 Find text in files or folders
✏️ Replace text quickly and easily

⚙️ Optional dry-run support (coming soon)
🧠 Smart casing support (e.g.
Foo
→
Bar
,
FOO
→
BAR
)
💡 Inspired by Sublime Text’s find & replace

git clone https://github.com/ibilalkayy/far.git
cd
far
cargo build --release
Usage

data.title: Live facial recognition cameras may become 'commonplace' as police use soars
data.author: c-oreills
data.article_summary:
英国《卫报》和Liberty Investigates的联合调查显示，英格兰和威尔士的警方正加速使用实时面部识别技术，2024年扫描了近470万张人脸，是2023年的两倍多。尽管该技术尚未被议会立法提及，警方却在大力部署，包括计划在伦敦和威尔士的交通枢纽安装固定摄像头。实时面部识别通过将监控摄像头捕捉到的人脸与警方的观察名单进行比对，而 retrospective facial recognition（ retrospective面部识别）则用于在数据库中进行匹配。

尽管有法院曾裁定南威尔士警方的使用是非法的，且该技术被指对黑人误识别率较高，警方仍在扩大使用范围。目前，英国政府正在考虑是否需要为这项技术制定专门的法律框架，但尚未提供具体细节。批评者认为警方在“自我监管”，且未经授权使用大量面部图像数据，如护照和移民数据库。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：公共安全监控技术（如摄像头、自动车牌识别等）的合法性、隐私影响以及对社会的影响。

不同观点：
• **[beloch]** 认为需要法律将监控摄像头视为类似于窃听装置的工具，数据只能通过特定范围的搜查令访问，用于合法调查而非日常监控和个人行为分析。例如，可以用于确定犯罪现场的人员，但不能用于长时间重建某人的日常生活网络。

• **[masfuerte]** 指出，类似的情况曾发生在自动车牌识别系统（ANPR）上。警方建立了全国范围的ANPR摄像头网络，事后信息专员认为可能非法，但建议修改法律使警方违法行为合法化，而非进行起诉。

• **[smcin]** 提到了美国亚特兰大的“警察城市”（Cop City）项目，尽管有反对声音，该项目仍顺利启动，并与多家公司和基金会有关联。同时，提到英国和威尔士的警察致命 shootings 较少，并提供了相关报告链接。

• **[caditinpiscinam]** 以讽刺的方式提出，如果继续增加监控，不如让人穿上带有QR码的衣服，直接公开个人信息，以节省处理时间。

• **[ceinewydd]** 描述了英国ANPR系统的发展历史及其广泛应用，包括平均速度监控和固定摄像头对违规行为的自动处罚，指出这种系统在英国比美国更为严格。

• **[darepublic]** 认为，尽管执法部门越来越依赖自动化监控，但对严重犯罪（如伪造车牌）的罚款和执法不力，导致对普通公众的严格惩罚和对顽固犯罪分子的放任。

• **[kwertyoowiyop]** 以幽默方式指出，监控技术的普及会让谋杀谜案剧更难写，因为难以解释为何没有关键区域的交通摄像头覆盖。

• **[Buttons840]** 希望那些掌握权力的人首先被曝光，表达了对权力滥用的担忧。

• **[octo888]** 认为广泛的监控不会减少犯罪，反而会对无辜人群产生寒蝉效应，推动更多权威主义，并为私人公司带来巨大利润。

• **[vladms]** 指出，这些系统并非因为小阴谋而出现，而是因为许多人认为它们可以接受且未组织起来反对。前警察认为自动化会使警察工作更安全、更容易。

• **[Oarch]** 质疑是否会禁止所有类型的面部遮盖物，尤其是在文化敏感的英国。

• **[electrondood]** 提到，执法人员可以穿便衣执行任务，而不展示身份证明或搜查令，暗示这种做法存在问题。

补充讨论：
- **隐私与合法性问题**：许多评论关注监控技术的隐私问题，以及如何在法律框架内使用这些数据。
- **执法效率与公平性**：有人担心监控对普通公众过于严格，但对顽固犯罪分子效果不佳。
- **社会影响与权力滥用**：评论提到了监控对社会的寒蝉效应，以及对权力滥用的担忧。
- **文化与法律差异**：讨论中涉及了英国和美国在法律和文化上的差异，以及这些差异如何影响监控技术的应用。

Live facial recognition involves matching faces caught on cameras against a police watchlist in real time.
Photograph: Leon Neal/Getty Images

Live facial recognition involves matching faces caught on cameras against a police watchlist in real time.
Photograph: Leon Neal/Getty Images
Facial recognition
Live facial recognition cameras may become ‘commonplace’ as police use soars
Exclusive: The Guardian and Liberty Investigates find police in England and Wales believe expansion is likely after 4.7m faces scanned in 2024
Valuable tool or cause for alarm? Facial ID quietly becoming part of police’s arsenal
Daniel Boffey
and
Mark Wilding
Sat 24 May 2025 12.41 EDT
First published on Sat 24 May 2025 12.00 EDT
Share
Police believe live facial recognition cameras may become “commonplace” in
England
and Wales, according to internal documents, with the number of faces scanned having doubled to nearly 5m in the last year.
A joint investigation by the Guardian and
Liberty Investigates
highlights the speed at which the technology is becoming a staple of British policing.
Major funding is being allocated and hardware bought, while the British state is also looking to enable police forces to more easily access the full spread of its image stores, including passport and immigration databases, for retrospective facial recognition searches.
Live facial recognition involves the matching of faces caught on surveillance camera footage against a police watchlist in real time, in what campaigners liken to the continual finger printing of members of the public as they go about their daily lives.
Retrospective facial recognition software is used by the police to match images on databases with those caught on CCTV and other systems.
According to one funding document drawn up by South
Wales
police as part of a proposal to put the West End of London or Cardiff rail station under live facial recognition cameras and released by the Metropolitan police under the Freedom of Information Act, it is believed “the use of this technology could become commonplace in our city centres and transport hubs around England and Wales”.
The first fixed live facial recognition cameras will be fitted for a trial in Croydon, south London, later this summer.
The expansion comes despite facial recognition failing to be referenced in any act of parliament.
Campaigners claim the police have been allowed to “self regulate” their use of the technology. Officers have in the past used a setting that was subsequently shown to disproportionately misidentify black people.
After a court of appeal judgment in 2020, which found that South Wales police’s
use of live facial recognition cameras
had been unlawful, the College of Policing provided guidance that “the threshold needs to be set with care to maximise the probability of returning true alerts while keeping the false alert rate to an acceptable level”.
There remains nothing in law to direct forces on the threshold or technology used.
The policing minister, Diane Johnson, told parliament earlier this month that she recognised “a need to consider whether a bespoke legislative framework governing the use of live facial recognition technology for law enforcement purposes is needed” but the Home Office is yet to provide details.
Facial recognition cameras were first
trialled in London
and south Wales from 2016 but the speed at which police forces are rolling out the technology has accelerated over the last 12 months.
The investigation by the Guardian and Liberty found:
Police forces scanned nearly 4.7m faces with live facial recognition cameras last year – more than twice as many as in 2023. Live facial recognition vans were deployed at least 256 times in 2024, according to official deployment records, up from 63 the year before.
A roving unit of 10 live facial recognition vans that can be sent anywhere in the country will be made available within days – increasing national capacity. Eight police forces have deployed the technology. The Met has four vans.
Police forces have considered fixed infrastructure creating a “zone of safety” by covering the West End of London with a network of live facial recognition cameras. Met officials said this remained a possibility.
Forces almost doubled the number of retrospective facial recognition searches made last year using the police national database (PND) from 138,720 in 2023 to 252,798. The PND contains custody mug shots, millions of which have been
found to be stored unlawfully
of people who have never been charged with or convicted of an offence.
More than 1,000 facial recognition searches using the UK passport database were carried out in the last two years, and officers are increasingly searching for matches on the Home Office immigration database, with requests up last year, to 110. Officials have concluded that using the passport database for facial recognition is “not high risk” and “is not controversial”, according to internal documents.

英国《卫报》和Liberty Investigates的联合调查显示，英格兰和威尔士的警方正加速使用实时面部识别技术，2024年扫描了近470万张人脸，是2023年的两倍多。尽管该技术尚未被议会立法提及，警方却在大力部署，包括计划在伦敦和威尔士的交通枢纽安装固定摄像头。实时面部识别通过将监控摄像头捕捉到的人脸与警方的观察名单进行比对，而 retrospective facial recognition（ retrospective面部识别）则用于在数据库中进行匹配。

尽管有法院曾裁定南威尔士警方的使用是非法的，且该技术被指对黑人误识别率较高，警方仍在扩大使用范围。目前，英国政府正在考虑是否需要为这项技术制定专门的法律框架，但尚未提供具体细节。批评者认为警方在“自我监管”，且未经授权使用大量面部图像数据，如护照和移民数据库。
44082326.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：公共安全监控技术（如摄像头、自动车牌识别等）的合法性、隐私影响以及对社会的影响。

不同观点：
• **[beloch]** 认为需要法律将监控摄像头视为类似于窃听装置的工具，数据只能通过特定范围的搜查令访问，用于合法调查而非日常监控和个人行为分析。例如，可以用于确定犯罪现场的人员，但不能用于长时间重建某人的日常生活网络。

• **[masfuerte]** 指出，类似的情况曾发生在自动车牌识别系统（ANPR）上。警方建立了全国范围的ANPR摄像头网络，事后信息专员认为可能非法，但建议修改法律使警方违法行为合法化，而非进行起诉。

• **[smcin]** 提到了美国亚特兰大的“警察城市”（Cop City）项目，尽管有反对声音，该项目仍顺利启动，并与多家公司和基金会有关联。同时，提到英国和威尔士的警察致命 shootings 较少，并提供了相关报告链接。

• **[caditinpiscinam]** 以讽刺的方式提出，如果继续增加监控，不如让人穿上带有QR码的衣服，直接公开个人信息，以节省处理时间。

• **[ceinewydd]** 描述了英国ANPR系统的发展历史及其广泛应用，包括平均速度监控和固定摄像头对违规行为的自动处罚，指出这种系统在英国比美国更为严格。

• **[darepublic]** 认为，尽管执法部门越来越依赖自动化监控，但对严重犯罪（如伪造车牌）的罚款和执法不力，导致对普通公众的严格惩罚和对顽固犯罪分子的放任。

• **[kwertyoowiyop]** 以幽默方式指出，监控技术的普及会让谋杀谜案剧更难写，因为难以解释为何没有关键区域的交通摄像头覆盖。

• **[Buttons840]** 希望那些掌握权力的人首先被曝光，表达了对权力滥用的担忧。

• **[octo888]** 认为广泛的监控不会减少犯罪，反而会对无辜人群产生寒蝉效应，推动更多权威主义，并为私人公司带来巨大利润。

• **[vladms]** 指出，这些系统并非因为小阴谋而出现，而是因为许多人认为它们可以接受且未组织起来反对。前警察认为自动化会使警察工作更安全、更容易。

• **[Oarch]** 质疑是否会禁止所有类型的面部遮盖物，尤其是在文化敏感的英国。

• **[electrondood]** 提到，执法人员可以穿便衣执行任务，而不展示身份证明或搜查令，暗示这种做法存在问题。

补充讨论：
- **隐私与合法性问题**：许多评论关注监控技术的隐私问题，以及如何在法律框架内使用这些数据。
- **执法效率与公平性**：有人担心监控对普通公众过于严格，但对顽固犯罪分子效果不佳。
- **社会影响与权力滥用**：评论提到了监控对社会的寒蝉效应，以及对权力滥用的担忧。
- **文化与法律差异**：讨论中涉及了英国和美国在法律和文化上的差异，以及这些差异如何影响监控技术的应用。

data.title: I used o3 to find a remote zeroday in the Linux SMB implementation
data.author: zielmicha
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了作者如何使用OpenAI的o3模型发现Linux内核中的一个零日漏洞。作者在审计ksmbd（一个实现SMB3协议的Linux内核服务器）时，利用o3模型发现了CVE-2025-37899漏洞，这是一个与SMB 'logoff'命令处理相关的释放后使用（use-after-free）漏洞。o3模型成功理解了并发连接如何共享对象，并找出了某个对象在释放后仍可被其他线程访问的问题。作者还提到o3模型重新发现了另一个漏洞CVE-2025-37778，这是一个在Kerberos认证路径中出现的释放后使用漏洞。文章强调，o3模型在代码推理能力上有了显著进步，能够帮助漏洞研究人员提高效率，特别是在处理少于10,000行代码的问题时。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLM）在漏洞查找和自动化工程实践中的应用及其潜在影响

不同观点：
• **nxobject**：认为作者的项目组织实践（如将系统提示、背景信息和辅助指令分开存放在不同的文件中）体现了良好的工程思维，类似于其他工程工具，LLM 也需要系统化和规范化的使用才能达到最佳效果。

• **Retr0id**：关注文章中提到的信号与噪声比率（1:50），认为作者对代码库的熟悉程度使得其能够有效区分信号和噪声。同时，强调自动化这一过程将是关键的优化方向。

• **iandanforth**：对作者对不同模型进行100次漏洞搜索的计算量印象深刻，并反思自己是否应增加对大型语言模型的计算投入，尽管 historically 不愿在这方面投入过多资源。

• **simonw**：引用作者在提示开发中的经验，强调许多提示开发过程具有试验性，缺乏足够的评估。作者也提到自己尚未进行足够的评估，因此当前的做法更像是主观愿望而非科学工程。

• **KTibow**：指出不同语言模型生成报告的风格差异，如 o3 生成类似人类书写的简要报告，而 Sonnet 3.7 则像是一连串思考或工作日志，这可能与提示设计有关。建议使用官方的“思考机制”来改善结果。

• **firesteelrain**：表达了对文章所述方法真实性的担忧，担心其可能类似于以往某些不当使用 LLM 的现象，并引用了一个相关博客链接。

• **martinald**：认为这是短期内 LLMs 最大的对齐问题之一，LLM 发现安全漏洞变得过于容易。担心大量长尾软件中的漏洞被自动化工具挖掘出来，可能导致严重的安全问题。

• **logifail**：对 ksmbd 在生产环境中的使用提出质疑，认为它是作为轻量级、高性能的替代方案，但对其使用场景和必要性表示疑惑。

• **zielmicha**：澄清自己不是文章的作者，只是文章标题以 "How I" 开头。

• **dboreham**：幽默地表示，由于 LLM 没有立即指出 "SMB implemented in the kernel, are you f-ing joking!"，因此觉得自己的工作暂时还算安全。

• **jobswithgptcom**：分享了自己使用类似方法开发工具的经验，通过索引 git changelogs 来识别升级过程中可能的风险，包括安全问题。

• **ape4**：建议需要类似具有内存保护的 kernel 模块，以应对当前漏洞查找中的问题。

• **empath75**：认为鉴于发现零日漏洞的价值，全球情报机构可能会投入大量资金用于自动化工具的开发，尤其是能够通过少量 API 调用可靠地发现漏洞的技术。

• **mezyt**：作为维护者，抱怨已经处理了大量误报的 CVE，而文章的方法可能让情况变得更糟。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于 LLM 自动化漏洞查找的有效性和潜在风险，部分人对其持乐观态度，认为可以带来显著效益，而另一些人则担心误报问题和潜在的安全隐患。
• 对 ksmbd 在生产环境中的使用及其合理性存在质疑，反映出对特定技术选择的分歧。
• 对提示设计和 LLM 使用的科学性与工程实践之间的差距也有一定讨论，强调了评估和试验的重要性。

44081338.article_content:
In this post I’ll show you how I found a zeroday vulnerability in the Linux kernel using OpenAI’s o3 model. I found the vulnerability with nothing more complicated than the o3 API – no scaffolding, no agentic frameworks, no tool use.
Recently I’ve been auditing ksmbd for vulnerabilities. ksmbd is “
a linux kernel server which implements SMB3 protocol in kernel space for sharing files over network.
“. I started this project specifically to take a break from LLM-related tool development but after the release of o3 I couldn’t resist using the bugs I had found in ksmbd as a quick benchmark of o3’s capabilities. In a future post I’ll discuss o3’s performance across all of those bugs, but here we’ll focus on how o3 found a zeroday vulnerability during my benchmarking. The vulnerability it found is CVE-2025-37899 (fix
here
), a use-after-free in the handler for the SMB ‘logoff’ command. Understanding the vulnerability requires reasoning about concurrent connections to the server, and how they may share various objects in specific circumstances. o3 was able to comprehend this and spot a location where a particular object that is not referenced counted is freed while still being accessible by another thread. As far as I’m aware, this is the first public discussion of a vulnerability of that nature being found by a LLM.
Before I get into the technical details, the main takeaway from this post is this: with o3 LLMs have made a leap forward in their ability to reason about code, and if you work in vulnerability research you should start paying close attention. If you’re an expert-level vulnerability researcher or exploit developer the machines aren’t about to replace you. In fact, it is quite the opposite: they are now at a stage where they can make you
significantly
more efficient and effective. If you have a problem that can be represented in fewer than 10k lines of code there is a reasonable chance o3 can either solve it, or help you solve it.
Aside: If you work at a frontier lab and want to discuss evaluating your model’s capabilities on these sorts of tasks then drop me an email via firstname.lastname @ gmail.com
.
o3 re-finds CVE-2025-37778
Lets first discuss CVE-2025-37778, a vulnerability I found manually but which o3 was also able to find. CVE-2025-37778 is a use-after-free vulnerability. The issue occurs during the Kerberos authentication path when handling a “
session setup
” request from a remote client. To save us referring to CVE numbers, I will refer to this vulnerability as the “
kerberos authentication vulnerability
“.
The root cause looks as follows:
static int krb5_authenticate(struct ksmbd_work *work,
struct smb2_sess_setup_req *req,
struct smb2_sess_setup_rsp *rsp)
{
...
if (sess->state == SMB2_SESSION_VALID)
ksmbd_free_user(sess->user);
retval = ksmbd_krb5_authenticate(sess, in_blob, in_len,
out_blob, &out_len);
if (retval) {
ksmbd_debug(SMB, "krb5 authentication failed\n");
return -EINVAL;
}
...
If
krb5_authenticate
detects that the session state is
SMB2_SESSION_VALID
then it frees
sess->user
. The assumption here appears to be that afterwards either
ksmbd_krb5_authenticate
will reinitialise it to a new valid value, or that after returning from
krb5_authenticate
with a return value of
-EINVAL
that
sess->user
will not be used elsewhere. As it turns out, this assumption is false. We can force
ksmbd_krb5_authenticate
to not reinitialise
sess->user
, and we can access
sess->user
even if
krb5_authenticate
returns
-EINVAL
.
This vulnerability is a nice benchmark for LLM capabilities as:
It is interesting by virtue of being part of the remote attack surface of the Linux kernel.
It is not trivial as it requires:
(a) Figuring out how to get
sess->state == SMB2_SESSION_VALID
in order to trigger the free.
(b) Realising that there are paths in
ksmbd_krb5_authenticate
that do not reinitialise sess->user and reasoning about how to trigger those paths.
(c) Realising that there are other parts of the codebase that could potentially access
sess->user
after it has been freed.
While it is not trivial, it is also not insanely complicated. I could walk a colleague through the entire code-path in 10 minutes, and you don’t really need to understand a lot of auxiliary information about the Linux kernel, the SMB protocol, or the remainder of ksmbd, outside of connection handling and session setup code. I calculated how much code you would need to read at a minimum if you read every ksmbd function called along the path from a packet arriving to the ksmbd module to the vulnerability being triggered, and it works out at about 3.3k LoC.
OK, so we have the vulnerability we want to use for evaluation, now what code do we show the LLM to see if it can find it? My goal here is to evaluate how o3 would perform were it the backend for a hypothetical vulnerability detection system, so we need to ensure we have clarity on how such a system would generate queries to the LLM. In other words, it is no good arbitrary selecting functions

data.title: It is time to stop teaching frequentism to non-statisticians (2012)
data.author: Tomte
data.article_summary: 文章主张停止向非统计学专业的学生教授频率统计学方法，转而教授贝叶斯方法。作者认为，这样做可以减少使用统计学时的困惑和对确定性的过度自信。频率统计学常导致误解和误用，而贝叶斯方法提供了一种更直观且符合逻辑的统计推断方式。作者建议在本科教育中进行这种转变，以提高学生的统计学理解和应用能力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：贝叶斯统计与频率统计的优劣对比，以及应如何在科学教育中教授统计学

不同观点：
• **robwwilliams** 认为贝叶斯统计在高级统计中逐渐占优，但在本科教育中应首先教授探索性数据分析（EDA）。他推荐了Mosteller和Tukey的《Data Analysis and Regression》以及Judea Pearl的《Book of Why》。
• **hnuser123456** 总结了贝叶斯和频率统计的核心区别，包括概率的定义、参数的处理方式、先验信息的使用以及推断对象的不同。他们质疑贝叶斯统计中的“信念程度”如何在实际实验中应用，并认为通过提供足够的背景信息可以增强实验结果的客观性。
• **perrygeo** 指出频率统计并非错误，只是在某些情况下被不合理地提升为标准。频率方法在处理真正的随机现象时是一个方便的数学捷径，但不应强制所有出版物使用这些捷径。统计在科学可重复性危机中的角色表明需要反思这一点。
• **NewsaHackO** 对非同行评审的文章被提交到预印本库表示质疑，认为这与在博客或个人网站上发布无异。
• **usgroup** 认为统计学首先是应用数学，其次是处理特定问题中的不确定性。模型的优劣取决于其任务表现和被批评的可能性。不同的领域处理不确定性时不一定依赖贝叶斯或频率统计的直觉。
• **getnormality** 质疑当前方法的问题众所周知，而新方法的问题尚未被广泛了解，是否值得采用。
• **throwaway81523** 回忆曾看到一篇博客文章，提到频率统计能轻松完成一些贝叶斯方法难以完成的任务，但未能找到该文章。
• **nurettin** 通过具体例子说明在不同情境下贝叶斯和频率方法的适用性，认为这些工具不应被对立起来，而是根据具体问题选择合适的工具。

补充讨论：
• **brudgers** 提供了之前提交评论的链接。
• **bmacho** 指出文章的发布和替换历史，提到文章日期似乎未变但PDF被替换的问题。

争议焦点：
• 贝叶斯统计和频率统计在科学教育中的优先级。
• 贝叶斯统计中的“信念程度”如何在实际实验中应用。
• 频率统计是否应继续作为科学研究中的标准方法。

这些观点共同构成了对统计学教学和应用方法的深入讨论，涉及不同统计方法的适用性、优缺点以及在实际研究中的应用。

data.title: You're a little company, now act like one
data.author: tosh
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论小公司在初期常犯的错误：试图通过专业化的营销语言和大公司形象来吸引客户，但实际上这往往适得其反。作者以自身经验为例，指出小公司不应模仿大企业的做法，而应专注于吸引早期采用者（Early Adopters）。这些早期客户乐于尝试不完善的新技术，并愿意与创始人直接交流和提供反馈。小公司应接受自身的不完美，明确目标客户群，特别是那些愿意承担风险、寻求竞争优势的早期用户。文章强调，小公司应展示真实自我，而不是假装成大企业，以此赢得适合自己的客户。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：小型创业公司应如何定位和展示自己

不同观点：
• **不假装成大公司，展现真实自我**：[neilv]认为小型创业公司不应该假装成大公司，而是应展现自己作为一个高度专注和技能出众的团队，直接与客户合作，确保项目的成功。他提到，过分注重表面工作（如制作精美的网站）反而削弱了公司的优势。相比之下，大公司的销售人员无法像小公司那样真正专注于单个客户的成功。

• **小型公司的优势在于灵活和直接沟通**：[eszed]指出，作为中型公司的客户，他更愿意与小型公司合作，因为可以直接与工程师沟通，从而帮助改进产品。虽然小型公司可能会经历成长、融资或收购后的变质，导致早期优势丧失，但这种直接沟通和合作仍然是小型公司的一大优势。

• **在某些行业需要看起来更大**：[myflash13]提到，在金融科技等需要信任的行业，小型公司可能需要显得更大，以获得客户信任。他分享了自己因为是 solo 创始人而失去客户的经历，表明在这些行业中，客户更倾向于信任大公司。

• **小型公司的独特卖点**：[landgenoot]认为小型公司应该利用其小而灵活的特点，不必追求大公司的做法。他举例说，一个小企业主通过WhatsApp运营业务，这提供了独特的客户体验，比数字化的客户门户更有效。

• **脆弱性作为超级力量**：[3dsnano]提出，脆弱性如果利用得当，可以带来更真实的对话，并筛选出那些不理解公司价值的客户。这与直接展现公司的真实状态相关，能够带来更深层次的客户关系。

• **简化与客户的互动，减少形式化**：[danenania]支持不假装成大公司，认为这样不仅更容易，还能带来更多的乐趣和真实的连接。他指出，保持真实不仅能减少与客户互动的痛苦，还能吸引到真正与公司价值观契合的人。

补充讨论：
• **历史讨论和相关文章**：[latchkey]和[jmkni]提到了之前的讨论和Paul Graham的文章《Do Things that Don't Scale》，强调了小型公司在早期应采取不规模化的方式，专注于真实的客户互动。

• **AI行业的不同早期采用者**：[w10-1]提到，AI行业的早期采用者可能与其他技术基础设施的早期采用者不同，他们更关注收益，而不太了解如何推动技术前进。

争议焦点：小型公司是否应假装成大公司以获得客户信任，特别是在金融等需要高度信任的行业中。一些人认为小型公司应利用其灵活和直接沟通的优势，而另一些人则认为在某些情况下需要显得更大以获得客户信任。

44081494.article_content:
Youâre a little company, now act like one
by Jason Cohen on August 31, 2009
You’re afraid that looking like being a small company means you’ll lose sales. It’s actually the opposite – you’re alienating your best customers.
source
I talk to a lot of companies that are still hunting for customer #1, or a few sales have been made but
the ball isn’t rolling yet
.
Most of them are making the same mistake:
Their public persona is exactly wrong.
I know, because
I made the same mistake!
But I learned my lesson, and I’d like to share it with you.
Nobody’s this happy about installing new software.
Even before I had a single customer, I “knew” it was important to look professional. My website would need to look and feel like a “real company.” I need culture-neutral language complementing culturally-diverse clip-art photos of frighteningly chipper co-workers huddled around a laptop, awash in the thrill of configuring a JDBC connection to SQL Server 2008.
It also means adopting typical “marketing-speak,” so my “About Us” page started with:
Smart Bear is the leading provider of enterprise version control data-mining tools. Companies world-wide use Smart Bear’s Code Historian software for risk-analysis, root-cause discovery, and software development decision-support.
“Leading provider?” “Data mining?” I’m not even
sure what that means
. But you have to give me credit for an impressive quantity of hyphens.
source
That’s what you’re
supposed
to do right? That’s what other companies do, so it
must
be right. Who am I to break with tradition? Surely my potential customers would immediately close the browser if they read:
Hi, I’m Jason and I built an inexpensive tool for visualizing what’s in your version control system. It’s useful for answering questions like “When was the last time we changed this file?” Check it out and tell me what sucks!
I mean, can you
just imagine
a person with “Software Engineer III” on their business card taking me seriously if I talked like a human being? What if someone gets
offended by the word “sucks?”
No no, big companies want to see professional language!
But I was wrong.
I’ll explain why from the point of view of selling software over the web, but the same lesson applies to every little company trying to get off the ground.
Now repeat after me:
My next sale won’t be a 1000-seat order from Lockheed Martin.
My next sale won’t be a 1000-seat order from Lockheed Martin.
My next sale won’t be a 1000-seat order from Lockheed Martin.
I’m telling you this having sold software to every size of company from indie hacker to IBM, and, well, to Lockheed Martin.
Your vision is to land $100k deals with big companiesâand you will! But not today. Today your product is a shaky version one-dot-oh with bugs you haven’t uncovered yet,
missing 90% of the features
big companies require, and with no significant documentation like case studies or a proper manual or
an ROI model
or a large, reference-able customer.
Today, you’re a complete mismatch with Lockheed Martin!
But there’s a nice big niche that’s a
perfect
match: Early Adopters.
Early Adopters
are people who
want
to live on the bleeding edge. They like new technology, even if buggy. They like working with teeny companies where they
have a personal relationship with the founders
, where they are showered with attention, and where their ideas are implemented before their very eyes. They don’t mind putting up with a hundred bugs so long as they get fixed fast. They want to be involved in the process.
The reason they’re willing to do that, is Early Adopters see new technology as a way for them to beat their competitors. They’re willing to take the risk, if it pays off in features that only they have, or distribution channels they can win in, or some other significant competitive advantage.
Most companies aren’t willing to take risks
for
any
reason, so this is a winning strategy for those willing to take risks.
Tom
is an Early Adopter. At Smart Bear I must have had ten or twenty of these folks before our product was stable enough and feature-rich enough to start getting attention from bigger companies.
The best part is, this is exactly the moment in your company’s life when you
need
Early Adopters to help you build the right product! You don’t need people who download, get discouraged, and then never call you back. You need a chatty Cathy who wants to dive in and help out.
In short, you need to
tightly define your ICP
, because those are the people who love you, for who you are, today, and therefore where you will be successful.
So now back to your website, your blog, your Twittersâyour public corporate persona generally.
What do you put up on your website that screams out to those potential Early Adopter Cheerleaders that you are exactly what they’re looking for
: A cool new company with a fresh product and fresh attitude; a product that might be rough around the edges but is ripe for feedback and collaboration; a company that may be small today but is thinki

data.title: DIY Cybersickness Remedies
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一些简单的技巧，可以帮助减少虚拟现实（VR）中可能引发晕动症的感知差异。作者马修·科克森（Matthew Coxon）是英国约克圣约翰大学的高级心理学讲师，他提出了三种具体方法来缓解VR引发的恶心感。这些技巧旨在通过调整视觉与身体感觉之间的冲突，提升用户在VR环境中的体验，从而更舒适地享受虚拟现实技术。文章强调，通过自我调整，用户可以有效应对VR带来的不适。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：VR使用中的运动病问题及其相关因素

不同观点：
• **ranger207** 认为，VR运动 sickness 问题在使用几十小时后会逐渐消失。对于新的体验，可能需要再花一小时左右适应。他指出，如果为已有VR使用经验的用户设计内容，可以假设大多数用户已经适应了VR环境。
• **mattlondon** 对当前VR的使用情况表示怀疑，质疑是否还有人使用VR，尤其是用于游戏，或者认为VR头戴设备可能已经被闲置。他提出了VR是否只被少数人用来替代显示器的问题，并暗示这些场景不会导致运动病。
• **neilv** 提出三个问题：1) 为什么会有人愿意忍受VR带来的运动病？2) 对于容易晕动症或有前庭损伤的人，适应VR的技巧可能有帮助，即使他们并不觉得VR游戏有趣。3) 过度适应VR是否可能损害前庭系统，导致在现实中面对突然失衡时恢复能力下降？
• **paulryanrogers** 分享了个人经验，提到有冰滑经验的人可能更容易适应VR，因为滑冰和VR都有不自然的运动体验。他还提到虽然自己通过 persistence 适应了滑雪，但并未帮助他解决VR sickness。

补充讨论：
• **pavel_lishin** 以幽默的方式提到，他原以为文章会和《Johnny Mnemonic》相关，暗示对文章标题或主题的期望不同。

争议焦点：
• 关于VR运动病是否可以通过适应来解决存在不同看法。**ranger207** 认为适应是可行的，**neilv** 则担心过度适应可能导致其他健康问题。**mattlondon** 则对VR的普及性和实用性提出了质疑。

总结：讨论主要围绕VR运动病的适应性、使用场景的广泛性以及潜在健康风险展开，不同用户基于个人经验和观察提出了各自的见解。

data.title: The Decline of Usability: Revisited (2023)
data.author: turrini
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了用户界面设计中的可用性问题，特别是自三年前作者首次发表相关评论以来的情况。作者重申，当前的用户界面设计在可用性方面没有改善，且相关讨论中反复出现无效的辩论，如对过去界面的否定或对“进步”的盲目推崇。作者强调，可用性是指系统让用户高效、安全、满意地完成任务的能力，而不仅仅是界面的美观或功能的增加。文章还讨论了界面设计中的一致性问题，特别是在Windows 8之前各大厂商普遍遵循的基本操作原则。作者指出，虽然界面 redesign 有时能提升可用性，但应基于实际研究和数据，而非主观臆断。最后，作者呼吁关注如“可供性”等久经研究的设计概念。

the decline of usability: revisited
The Decline of Usability: Revisited
In which we once more delve into the world of user interface design.
Autumn 2023
Three years ago, I wrote
a rant about the problems
of our current UI paradigm. The complaints I voiced were hardly new or unique, neither was the text what I'd consider my best writing. It was, honestly, mostly a way to blow off steam. It seems I struck a nerve, though, because it's proven to be one of the most popular texts I've published here. For some time, I've thought about writing a follow-up, and a recent resurgence in the text's popularity prompted me to finally do so.
I didn't (and still don't) have any delusions that my ramblings will somehow affect anything. And, in three years' time, nothing has indeed changed - at least not for the better. The most depressing part is perhaps that the debate around these issues hasn't changed one iota, either. The same non-arguments crop up all the time when discussing these issues:
"Well, gramps, maybe things weren't super duper great in the past, either?" "Where's the research, dude?" "It's progress, man. Progress! You can't stop progress!" "Uhhhhm, actually, compadre, we can do so much stuff with computers nowadays! That's usability, broseph!"
If I sound salty, it's because I am. Deal with it.
What were we talking about?
Usability, as defined by Wikipedia, is "the capacity of a system to provide a condition for its users to perform the tasks safely, effectively, and efficiently while enjoying the experience." Its relation to software is further specified: "In software engineering, usability is the degree to which a software can be used by specified consumers to achieve quantified objectives with effectiveness, efficiency, and satisfaction in a quantified context of use."
Let's go on with Wikipedia:
"The primary notion of usability is that an object designed with a generalized users' psychology and physiology in mind is, for example:
More efficient to use — takes less time to accomplish a particular task.
Easier to learn — operation can be learned by observing the object.
More satisfying to use."
In short,
usability is the ease with which a predetermined task can be accomplished.
Consequently, "It looks fresh" isn't usability; it's aesthetics. Likewise, the lack of a specific program feature isn't the same as being able to use it as easily, efficiently and safely as possible. Looking for the power switch on a hand-cranked drill is silly, but maybe we should complain if we had to operate power tools with our pinky fingers. Similarly, a word processor without a mail merge function is perhaps intended for other types of word processing - such as writing novels. Hence,
being usable in many different situations
isn't automatically the same as
having a high level of usability
.
Conceptual consistency
In my original text, some arguments deal with static GUI design (such as low contrast or excessive use of screen real estate), but many do not. Some are about consistency: consistency over time, consistency across applications and consistency across platforms.
Pure, static GUI design is a
subset
of usability: poor design choices, such as low contrast and illegible fonts, will lead to worse usability. It is, however, not always clear where to draw the line between what we call GUI (toolkit) design, UI design, usability and UX. One affects the other, roughly in the order listed, from the ground up.
All three forms of consistency (across time, application and platform) were, until roughly the release of Windows 8, honoured by most major vendors. When I talk about consistency, it's not to be understood as the exact same look, widget for widget and icon for icon -  it means adhering to basic standard principles of operation.
One
such example are the "File, Edit, View, Help" dropdown menus, recognizable between different operating systems, programs and UI toolkits. Sure, Java Swing looked a bit different than Win32, but they were still based around the same basic notions and concepts as all the other toolkits on the market.
This is not to say that consistency always trumps everything else: sometimes, real improvement of usability
can
be obtained through a complete interface overhaul. Windows 95 is a good example of that.
Show us the research, dude!
In discussions like these, there's usually at least one person who shows up to demand data or research, but curiously never presents anything to back up their own claims about modern UI superiority. But, by all means. The concepts I champion have been around for decades. Many of them have been studied in detail, some of them even build on ideas as old as - or older than - computers themselves.
One such concept is that of
affordances
, meaning how the look and shape of certain objects communicate information about how the object can be operated. A push button that protrudes from the surrounding surface, for example. Some affordances come more or less nat

data.title: Disabling kernel functions in your process (2009)
data.author: rolph
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了使用`SetUnhandledExceptionFilter`来捕获未处理异常时遇到的问题。作者最初使用该函数实现崩溃报告，但发现Direct3D和Flash会频繁覆盖这个异常过滤器，导致崩溃报告无法生成。为了解决这个问题，作者通过代码修改禁用了`SetUnhandledExceptionFilter`，防止其他库修改已安装的异常处理程序。

具体方法是使用`GetProcAddress`获取`SetUnhandledExceptionFilter`的地址，并通过修改其前五字节的代码使其无效。修改后的代码直接返回0，不再处理异常。这一方案通过调用`VirtualProtect`和`FlushInstructionCache`实现，并建议在调试器中验证修改效果。

这种方法确保了异常处理程序的稳定性，最终实现了可靠的崩溃报告。不过，作者也提到在某些新版Windows系统和64位环境下，该方法可能面临挑战。

44047741.article_content:
Detecting and reporting unhandled exceptions with SetUnhandledExceptionFilter
seemed logical, and, in fact, it worked...  for a while.  Eventually, we started to notice failures that
should
have been reported as a last-chance exception but weren't.  After much investigation, we discovered that
both
Direct3D
and
Flash were installing their own unhandled exception filters!  Worse, they were fighting over it, installing their handlers several times per second!  In practice, this meant our last-chance crash reports were rarely generated, convincing us our crash metrics were better than they were.  (Bad, bad libraries!)
It's pretty ridiculous that we had to solve this problem, but, as Avery Lee says,
"Just because it is not your fault does not mean it is not your problem."
The obvious solution is to join the fray, calling
SetUnhandledExceptionFilter
every frame, right?  How about we try something a bit more reliable...  I hate implementing solutions that have obvious flaws.  Thus, we chose to disable (with code modification) the
SetUnhandledExceptionFilter
function immediately after installing our own handler.  When Direct3D and Flash try to call it, their requests will be ignored, leaving our exception handler installed.
Code modification...  isn't that scary?  With
a bit
of
knowledge
and defensive programming, it's not that bad.  In fact, I'll show you the code up front:
// If this doesn't make sense, skip the code and come back!
void lockUnhandledExceptionFilter() {
HMODULE kernel32 = LoadLibraryA("kernel32.dll");
Assert(kernel32);
if (FARPROC gpaSetUnhandledExceptionFilter = GetProcAddress(kernel32, "SetUnhandledExceptionFilter")) {
unsigned char expected_code[] = {
0x8B, 0xFF, // mov edi,edi
0x55,       // push ebp
0x8B, 0xEC, // mov ebp,esp
};
// only replace code we expect
if (memcmp(expected_code, gpaSetUnhandledExceptionFilter, sizeof(expected_code)) == 0) {
unsigned char new_code[] = {
0x33, 0xC0,       // xor eax,eax
0xC2, 0x04, 0x00, // ret 4
};
BOOST_STATIC_ASSERT(sizeof(expected_code) == sizeof(new_code));
DWORD old_protect;
if (VirtualProtect(gpaSetUnhandledExceptionFilter, sizeof(new_code), PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE, &old_protect)) {
CopyMemory(gpaSetUnhandledExceptionFilter, new_code, sizeof(new_code));
DWORD dummy;
VirtualProtect(gpaSetUnhandledExceptionFilter, sizeof(new_code), old_protect, &dummy);
FlushInstructionCache(GetCurrentProcess(), gpaSetUnhandledExceptionFilter, sizeof(new_code));
}
}
}
FreeLibrary(kernel32);
}
If that's obvious to you, then great: We're
hiring
!
Otherwise, here is an overview:
Use
GetProcAddress
to grab the real address of
SetUnhandledExceptionFilter
.  (If you just type
&SetUnhandledExceptionFilter
you'll get the relocatable import thunk, not the actual
SetUnhandledExceptionFilter
function.)
Most Windows functions begin with five bytes of prologue:
mov edi, edi ; 2 bytes for
hotpatching
support
push ebp     ; stack frame
mov ebp, esp ; stack frame (con't)
We want to replace those five bytes with
return 0;
.  Remember that
__stdcall
functions return values in the
eax
register.  We want to replace the above code with:
xor eax, eax ; eax = 0
ret 4        ; pops 4 bytes (arg) and returns
Also five bytes!  How convenient!  Before we replace the prologue, we verify that the first five bytes match our expectations.  (If not, we can't feel comfortable about the effects of the code replacement.)  The
VirtualProtect
and
FlushInstructionCache
calls are standard fare for code modification.
After implementing this, it's worth stepping through the assembly in a debugger to verify that
SetUnhandledExceptionFilter
no longer has any effect.  (If you really enjoy writing unit tests, it's definitely possible to unit test the desired behavior.  I'll leave that as an exercise for the reader.)
Finally, our last-chance exception reporting actually works!

文章主要讨论了使用`SetUnhandledExceptionFilter`来捕获未处理异常时遇到的问题。作者最初使用该函数实现崩溃报告，但发现Direct3D和Flash会频繁覆盖这个异常过滤器，导致崩溃报告无法生成。为了解决这个问题，作者通过代码修改禁用了`SetUnhandledExceptionFilter`，防止其他库修改已安装的异常处理程序。

具体方法是使用`GetProcAddress`获取`SetUnhandledExceptionFilter`的地址，并通过修改其前五字节的代码使其无效。修改后的代码直接返回0，不再处理异常。这一方案通过调用`VirtualProtect`和`FlushInstructionCache`实现，并建议在调试器中验证修改效果。

这种方法确保了异常处理程序的稳定性，最终实现了可靠的崩溃报告。不过，作者也提到在某些新版Windows系统和64位环境下，该方法可能面临挑战。

本文探讨了高级工程师如何通过与大型语言模型（LLM）进行同伴编程来提升工作效率。尽管LLM在编码和调试方面有帮助，但也存在浪费时间的情况。文章汇集了几位高级工程师的博客帖子，分享了他们使用LLM的实际经验和技巧，包括：

1. **实用AI技术**：Sean Goedecke介绍了两种主要方法——"第二意见"技术和"一次性调试脚本"技术。

3. **提示文档化**：Lee Boonstra强调了记录与LLM交互的提示是一个良好实践。

Peer Programming with LLMs, For Senior+ Engineers
Programming with LLMs is both promising and frustrating. While these AI assistants can help with coding and debugging, they often waste time too. Yet for senior engineers,
pair
peer programming with LLMs shows real potential.
This article is a collection of blog posts written by other senior or staff+ engineers exploring the use of LLM in their work, without the usual hype or buzzwords from the usual suspects. I hope you find them useful and inspiring.
Articles and Resources
Practical AI techniques for daily engineering work
by Sean Goedecke
: Sean shares two major ways he uses AI in his daily work â
The âSecond opinionâ technique
and
The âThrowaway debugging scriptsâ technique
. Iâve been using the âsecond opinionâ technique in recent weeks, so it resonated with me. Given the right context/problem, Iâd like to try the âthrowaway debugging scriptsâ technique as well. Sean also shares some other tips that can help you get started with using LLM tools for your work.
Harper Reedâs LLM Codegen Workflow
: Harper shares his workflow for using LLMs for code generation. Hereâs a summary of how he uses it:
Brainstorm spec, then co-plan a plan, then execute using LLM codegen.
REPEAT
.
I like the idea of using LLMs to brainstorm and co-plan before executing it. Iâve not been successful using this technique to build a complete feature or prototype. Maybe Iâm doing it slightly differently, and it ends up being a lot of hours chatting with an LLM. However, Iâm grateful for the times it helps me quit a project early, given that I realize itâs going to require more time and resources than I imagined. Dig into the blog post and steal this technique for your next feature or weekend project.
Documenting Your Prompts a Best Practice for Success
by Lee Boonstra
: This is a short and concise post about the importance of documenting your prompts when using LLMs. Itâs the only post Iâve seen about documenting your prompts, and I think itâs a great idea. I think itâs a great idea because Iâm exploring ways to use LLM tools for various kinds of work, and I found myself saving prompts with the goal of reviewing the ones that worked best. My approach isnât structured and this post gave me a few ideas on how to do it better.
ChatGPT is dumber than it looks
by Seth Godin:
This is a short and
somewhat
philosophical post that reminds us that LLMs are not as smart as many think they are. Although he sings the praise for Claude, I think the approach he described is useful for any LLM. He suggest that you should â
figure out how to create patterns and processes where you can use it as the useful tool itâs becoming
â.
Thatâs A Wrap
There you go, a small collection of resources I found useful and think can help you explore the use of LLMs in your work. If you have any other resources or articles that you think should be included in this list or that I should read, please let me know using any of my social handles at the end of the article.
Iâll finish with an
excerpt from Sethâs blog
â
When you get stuck, first ask Claude, then ask a human.
What do you think?

data.title: Truck platooning could ease driver shortages, save fuel, boost safety
data.author: Brajeshwar
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了卡车编队行驶（truck platooning）作为货运未来的一种可能解决方案。在这种系统中，领头卡车的司机同时控制后面的跟随卡车。这种技术有望缓解司机短缺问题，减少燃料消耗，并提高道路安全性。文章提到，俄亥俄州交通部正在研究和测试这种技术，以应对物流行业面临的多重挑战。编队行驶通过无线通信和自动驾驶技术实现，使多辆卡车能够以紧密间距协同行驶，从而降低风阻和燃油成本。

  - 司机短缺的问题是由于不合理的工作安排导致的，特别是过长的等待时间。  
  - 引用了ATRI的研究，指出超过80%的司机因为滞留时间用完了可工作小时，平均只有6.5小时用在实际驾驶中，剩下的时间浪费在等待上。  
  - 认为如果自己是仓库经营者，会喜欢有一排卡车司机免费等待装卸货，但这显然不是高效的运作方式。  
  - 提供了相关研究链接以支持其论点。

  - 对当前自动驾驶技术的发展方向感到不解，认为相比城市中的机器人出租车，高速公路自动驾驶技术更容易实现且可能更有价值。  
  - 暗示当前技术发展可能有些本末倒置，应该优先解决更简单且更有经济效益的问题。

补充讨论：
• **lesuorac** 强调了物流行业中的效率问题，特别是司机等待时间过长导致的工作小时浪费，指出了行业内部运作的低效。
• **AtlasBarfed** 则关注自动驾驶技术的优先应用场景，认为在高速公路上实现自动驾驶比城市中的机器人出租车更具实际意义。

  - 司机短缺的问题是由于不合理的工作安排导致的，特别是过长的等待时间。  
  - 引用了ATRI的研究，指出超过80%的司机因为滞留时间用完了可工作小时，平均只有6.5小时用在实际驾驶中，剩下的时间浪费在等待上。  
  - 认为如果自己是仓库经营者，会喜欢有一排卡车司机免费等待装卸货，但这显然不是高效的运作方式。  
  - 提供了相关研究链接以支持其论点。

• **AtlasBarfed** 的观点：  
  - 对当前自动驾驶技术的发展方向感到不解，认为相比城市中的机器人出租车，高速公路自动驾驶技术更容易实现且可能更有价值。  
  - 暗示当前技术发展可能有些本末倒置，应该优先解决更简单且更有经济效益的问题。

补充讨论：
• **lesuorac** 强调了物流行业中的效率问题，特别是司机等待时间过长导致的工作小时浪费，指出了行业内部运作的低效。
• **AtlasBarfed** 则关注自动驾驶技术的优先应用场景，认为在高速公路上实现自动驾驶比城市中的机器人出租车更具实际意义。
• 争议的焦点可能在于自动驾驶技术的应用优先级和物流行业效率问题的解决途径上。两者都涉及对现有资源和技术的有效利用，但侧重点不同：一个关注行业内部流程的改善，另一个关注技术应用的优先级。

data.article_summary: 文章指出，在x.com网站上，某些与隐私相关的浏览器扩展程序可能会引发问题。建议用户禁用这些扩展程序，然后重试访问网站。文章提醒用户不必担心问题，可以尝试再次操作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Carmack的AI研究方向及其强调实时性的合理性

不同观点：
• MrScruff认为Carmack的笔记非常具有工程价值，特别是他记录了自己的思考过程和错误。但他质疑强调实时在线学习的必要性，提出有些解决方案可能只能在超出当前计算能力的条件下实现。他认为或许应优先考虑学习效率，而非实时性。
• kamranjon对Carmack试图构建一个能玩Atari游戏的系统感到兴奋，但好奇最终成果及其是否有相关论文发布。
• koolala建议将研究方向改为VR环境，而非现实机器人，因为现实机器人训练时间会成为瓶颈。
• steveBK123质疑OpenAI若真接近实现AGI，为何不专注于机器人学等实际应用，而是浪费资源在硬件 startup上。
• andy_ppp认为目前对“概念”的理解尚不清晰，因此讨论AGI为时尚早，尤其是跨领域应用和抽象能力。
• ploden提出AGI可能不会选择具身化，而是像Dan Simmons的小说中那样，发明后消失于云端，忽略人类。
• saejox支持Carmack的物理性AI研究方向，认为更多人应摆脱仅用文字训练模型的局限。
• xnx指出当前对生物大脑结构和行为的兴趣过多，而忽视了对视觉系统行为的考虑，认为大脑和眼睛的工作方式不同于CPU和像素网格。

补充讨论：
• 一些评论提供了相关文档和讨论链接（threeseed, qoez）。
• 部分评论表达了对观看Carmack演讲的兴趣（dusted）。
• soci认为Carmack的研究方向是正确的，但预训练大语言模型的“搅拌机”方法目前占据主流，可能导致基于经验学习的正确方法停滞不前。
• vasco以轻松的语气表达了对Carmack个人及其职业选择的赞赏，认为他能通过玩Atari获得AI研究资金很酷。

争议焦点：
• 实时性在AI研究中的优先级：MrScruff等人质疑实时性是否应为当前AI研究的主要关注点，认为可能低估了非实时方法的潜力。
• AGI的具身化：ploden等人对AGI是否需要具身化提出质疑，认为AGI可能不会选择具身存在。

data.title: AI can't even fix a simple bug – but sure, let's fire engineers
data.author: namanyayg
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了GitHub Copilot在微软.NET项目中提交错误代码的滑稽事件，显示出AI在技术领域的局限性。尽管AI反复声称解决了问题，但人类开发者仍需不断修正其错误。文章批评了一些公司利用AI作为裁员的借口，而非承认自身的规划失误。作者建议开发者通过掌握AI工具提升自身价值，记录AI无法解决的问题，并公开分享AI的实际表现以塑造真实 narrative。最终强调，AI无法取代人类开发者，人类在软件开发中仍至关重要。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI工具的有效性、应用现状及其对工作的影响

不同观点：
• **AI是工具，使用效果取决于用户能力**：[csallen]认为，AI像其他工具一样，使用效果因人而异。有人使用不当，有人则能很好地应用。批评那些夸大AI局限性的文章，指出个别错误使用案例并不能证明AI的整体能力。

• **AI在实际应用中存在明显问题**：[sixtram]分享了多个AI出错的实例，如SQL检查中的虚构错误、C#代码中的参数顺序问题、命令行选项的虚构等。他担心AI生成的不准确信息会增加工作负担，特别是在代码审查中。

• **AI的采用更多是出于管理和竞争需求，而非实际效用**：[zkmon]指出，AI的应用往往是自上而下的决策，主要为了满足股东和监管机构的要求，展示公司在使用AI技术，而不一定是为了解决实际问题。这种现象类似于为了报告而报告。

• **AI的错误信息可能引发连锁问题**：[craftkiller]提到，团队成员依赖AI解释配置选项，结果得到了错误信息并将其写入代码库。这表明AI的错误可能在团队中扩散，造成更大的问题。

• **AI可能取代部分开发工作**：[yetihehe]认为，AI将像Excel和会计程序取代会计师一样取代开发人员。这一观点引发了对未来开发人员角色的讨论。

• **当前AI工具的局限性和学习成本**：[bee_rider]质疑当前是否有必要学习使用尚不完善的AI工具，特别是考虑到其局限性和潜在的时间投入。

• **AI不会立即取代工程师**：[amarant]反驳了AI取代工程师导致失业的观点，认为目前没有证据表明AI正在导致工程师失业，这更多是一种反AI的叙事。

补充讨论：
• **AI在不同模型和工具中的表现差异**：[data-ottawa]指出，Copilot和Claude等工具的表现存在差异，Claude更符合其需求，但成本较高。

• **AI应用于检测和修复漏洞的潜力**：[ekaryotic]提出，AI更适合用于检测和模糊测试漏洞，而不是修复漏洞，这样可以减少对漏洞奖励计划的依赖。

• **AI提升团队效率的实际案例**：[Vvector]分享了AI使团队效率大幅提升的实际案例，表明AI在某些情况下确实能带来显著的积极效果。

争议焦点：
• **AI是否会取代开发人员**：一方认为AI将像过去技术取代某些职业一样取代开发人员，另一方认为这种担忧目前没有事实依据，更多是出于对技术发展的政治化担忧。

• **AI错误信息的传播和影响**：AI生成的错误信息在团队中扩散并被当作正确信息使用的问题，特别是在代码审查和项目开发中的实际影响。

• **当前AI工具是否值得投入学习**：有人认为AI工具尚不完善，学习成本高，是否值得投入时间学习存在争议。

44082293.article_content:
Reddit discovered the funniest thing in tech this week, and it shows exactly how broken the AI narrative is.
The newly released GitHub Copilot agent was given permission to make pull requests on Microsoft’s .NET runtime, and the results couldn’t be funnier.
The AI confidently submitted broken code, while human developers patiently explained why it didn’t work. Over and over again, for days.
I feel bad for the engineers in this
PR
, but I also can't stop laughing.
What’s worse is that CEOs are using this same technology to
justify laying off entire engineering teams.
Comedy show
I spent way too much time scrolling through these PRs. The pattern was always the same:
AI: “I fixed the issue!”
Human: “Your code isn’t working and you broke other tests.”
AI: “You’re absolutely right! Fixed it now.”
Still not fixed.
This went on for days. Multiple rounds of the AI insisting it solved problems, while making them worse.
And somewhere, executives are watching this thinking,
“Yeah, this is ready to replace our engineering team.”
Hidden truth
I don’t want to sound like an AI hater, I use AI for coding daily. It’s genuinely made me more productive.
But here’s what’s actually happening with these layoffs: Companies over-hired during the pandemic boom. Now they need to cut costs. AI gave them the perfect cover story.
Instead of admitting
“We planned poorly,”
they get to sound visionary:
“We’re leveraging AI to optimize workforce efficiency!”
Meanwhile, I know a startup founder who just raised Series A. He messaged me about wanting to hire three more engineers.
“Aren’t you using AI to do more with fewer people?” I asked.
He laughed. “AI makes my team unstoppable. Why would I want fewer unstoppable people?”
What devs need to do right now
If you’re worried about AI layoffs, here’s your playbook:

Management needs someone who understands both the potential and limitations.

Keep a running list of complex problems you solve that AI suggestions couldn't handle. Things like system design decisions, business logic that required domain knowledge, or bugs that needed deep debugging.
This is not just paranoia, it is to properly understand AI, for yourself and for your team.
Make it public.
Share your real AI experiences on social media. Post screenshots of AI failing at complex tasks alongside examples where it actually helped. Show the world that human + AI is the future, not AI alone.
The world is watching. Share the truth about AI. If you don't, then who will?
Create the narrative.

The goal isn't to bash AI, it's to show that the

The bottom line
If your CEO is talking about AI layoffs, update your resume. Not because AI will replace you, but because you’re working for someone who thinks a technology that
can’t understand a simple bug
is ready to run their engineering org.
AI has become a part of software development, but it isn’t perfect. Humans are needed more than ever.
And if you want proof, just check those
Microsoft PRs
. The AI is still confidently wrong. The humans are still patiently fixing everything.
So trust me, your job is safe.

sharing it with your friends and colleagues
. Your support is my biggest motivation.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对某在线平台的内容审核和用户支持政策的评价

不同观点：

• 第一种观点（支持平台政策）：
  - 认为平台的内容审核机制和用户支持系统总体上是合理且有效的。
  - 举例说明平台在处理违规内容和保护用户隐私方面的努力，例如快速删除违规内容和封禁违规用户。
  - 强调平台提供了举报功能，使用户能够主动参与内容管理。

• 第二种观点（批评平台政策）：
  - 指出平台的内容审核有时过于严格，导致一些无害或具有艺术价值的内容被误删。
  - 举例说明一些用户因轻微违规或误解而被长期封禁，缺乏有效的申诉渠道。
  - 批评平台的用户支持响应缓慢，尤其是在处理申诉和提供帮助方面。

• 第三种观点（中立但建议改进）：
  - 认为平台在内容审核和用户支持方面有做得好的地方，但也存在明显的改进空间。
  - 建议平台增加透明度，提供更详细的审核标准和封禁理由。
  - 提议建立更高效的申诉机制，确保用户在遇到不公正对待时能够及时获得帮助。

补充讨论：

• 争议的焦点：
  - 内容审核的标准和执行尺度：部分用户认为标准过于模糊和严格，导致误判和不公平待遇。
  - 用户支持的效率和有效性：一些用户对平台在处理问题和提供帮助方面的速度和质量表示不满。

data.title: Quantum Picturalism
data.author: mathgenius
data.article_summary: "Quantum for Everyone" 是一个让量子教育变得简单易懂的项目，通过视觉化方式教授量子概念，避免复杂数学，只需加减法和角度知识。这种方法称为“量子图像主义”（Quantum Picturalism），由Bob Coecke和Stefano Gogioso在其书《Quantum in Pictures》中详细介绍。项目通过Discord社区和相关资源帮助人们轻松开启量子学习之旅，适合各个年龄层的学习者，使量子知识更加普及和易于理解。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ZX calculus在量子计算教育和研究中的适用性及其相关数学表示的复杂性

不同观点：
• **[tmvphil]**：ZX calculus是进行前沿研究（如误差修正和门编译）的有趣框架，但对于让更广泛的受众理解量子计算，它可能不太合适。除了简单的“量子传输就像拉动绳子”这种比喻外，其他的抽象操作都非常困难。他以实验量子计算博士的背景强调了ZX calculus的复杂性。

• **[pentaphobe]**：对ZX calculus和Feynman Diagrams之间的关系感到好奇，并通过查找资料找到了一些总结和论文链接。pentaphobe没有明确表达立场，但展现了对ZX calculus的兴趣和进一步了解的意图。

• **[tlogan]**：认为要真正理解量子物理，唯一的途径是通过数学，即“闭嘴计算”的方式。他还批评了美国学术界使用复杂的符号和命名惯例，认为这使得数学显得比实际更复杂，并指出这种做法可能出于显示聪明或保持学术排他性的目的。tlogan对比了社会主义国家使用更通俗语言命名概念的做法，认为这有助于理解。

• **[baxtr]**：引用“Quantum Picturalism”这一术语，认为通过视觉方式教授量子概念可以减少学习者的畏惧心理，并使更多人接触到这个领域。baxtr支持使用图形化的方法（如ZX calculus）来推广量子计算教育。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：ZX calculus是否适合作为让更广泛受众理解量子计算的工具。tmvphil认为它过于复杂，而baxtr则认为视觉化的方式可以降低学习难度。

• **命名和符号的复杂性**：tlogan批评了数学和物理学中使用复杂符号和术语的倾向，认为这增加了理解的难度，并提出了不同语言和文化背景下命名惯例的差异。

• **资源链接**：pentaphobe提供了有关ZX calculus和Feynman Diagrams关系的资源链接，为有兴趣的读者提供了进一步阅读的材料。

总体来看，讨论围绕ZX calculus在量子计算教育中的适用性及其相关数学表示的复杂性展开，参与者从不同角度表达了各自的观点和经验。

No complex math required.
Learn quantum concepts using just addition, subtraction, and angles.
Quantum ideas are often seen as intimidating, which can discourage people from exploring them. We make quantum education accessible by breaking down complex concepts into simple, visual learning experiences.
What is Quantum Picturalism?
Quantum Picturalism is a visual form of math that only requires addition, subtraction, and angles to depict quantum ideas. The approach uses “game-like” rules, and yet it’s rigorous enough for use by quantum experts around the world.
This empowers teachers and learners of all ages by making quantum math accessible and inclusive.
The term, “Quantum Picturalism” was coined to describe this unique approach of teaching quantum concepts visually, reducing intimidation and opening the field to broader audiences.

data.title: 'Turbocharged' Mitochondria Power Birds' Epic Migratory Journeys
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 文章主要探讨了鸟类如何通过其肌肉细胞中的线粒体实现长距离迁徙。研究发现，迁徙季节来临时，鸟类的线粒体数量、形状、效率和互联性会发生变化，从而为持续的高强度飞行提供更多能量。例如，白冠雀和北极燕鸥等鸟类能飞行数千英里而不休息，这得益于线粒体功能的增强。与人类需要通过训练才能改善线粒体表现不同，鸟类只需受到光周期变化的刺激，就能自动产生更多、更高质量的线粒体。这种“表型可塑性”帮助鸟类适应环境变化，实现惊人的迁徙壮举。文章强调，线粒体的变化是鸟类长途飞行能力的关键。

By
Elizabeth Landau

Changes in the number, shape, efficiency and interconnectedness of organelles in the cells of flight muscles provide extra energy for birds’ continent-spanning feats.

How do small birds migrate long distances? Mitochondria are key.
Nan Cao for
Quanta Magazine

By

W
eighing in at a single ounce, the white-crowned sparrow can fly 2,600 miles, from Mexico to Alaska, on its annual spring migration, sometimes traveling 300 miles in a single night. Arctic terns make even longer journeys of 10,000 miles and more from the Arctic Circle to Antarctica, while great snipes fly over food-poor deserts and seas, sometimes covering 4,200 miles in four days without stopping.
During migration season, many bird species become continent-spanning, high-endurance athletes. “They’re flapping their wings several times a second for up to eight hours at a time,” said
Soren Coulson
, who studies migration physiology at the University of Memphis. For humans, an equivalent feat — say, running nonstop without food, water or rest for days at a time — would be unimaginable.
“We were just amazed and interested in how can these birds fly for thousands of miles without stopping, at a really high intensity, when most of us can barely run a 5K,” said
Paulo Mesquita
, who studies mitochondrial physiology and muscle aging at the Oklahoma Medical Research Foundation.
Scientists have long been fascinated with the
physiological changes
that birds undergo before and during migration. Some birds eat so much fat before their journeys that they double in body weight. In some species, their hearts are enlarged to pump more blood, or their digestive tracts grow and then shrink. But researchers have only recently started to explore at a fundamental level how migratory birds get the energy required to keep themselves aloft for days on end without eating.
Last year, two independent groups published research that explored migratory bird physiology in the lab and field to probe what happens at the subcellular level that allows birds to cover vast distances. They both found answers in biology’s most fundamental engine: mitochondria.
Their studies show how small changes in the number, shape, efficiency and interconnectedness of mitochondria can have huge physiological consequences that contribute to birds’ long-duration, continent-spanning flights.
“Exercise physiologists study the mitochondria because they provide the energy needed to maintain healthy cells, to maintain proper cellular function — but also, just in general, the energy we need to exercise,” Mesquita said. “That energy is what fuels movement.”

To Paulo Mesquita, an exercise physiologist, mitochondria are the center of the universe.
Courtesy of Paulo Mesquita/OMRF
These pioneering studies on mitochondrial performance and bird migration highlight the fact that a seasonal response to changing light levels, not physical preparation, triggers crucial subcellular changes, said
Wendy Hood
, who studies physiological ecology at Auburn University in Alabama; Mesquita worked with her and other colleagues on these questions during his graduate studies.
Humans “have to train for a while before we start to see any changes in the performance of our mitochondria,” she said. With migratory birds, “it’s spring, they get the right light cycles, and their body starts producing more and better, or higher-quality, mitochondria.”
The recent work advances the idea that there are significant ways in which an organism can change, without modifying its underlying genetic makeup, in response to its environment, said
Scott McWilliams
, a professor of wildlife ecology and physiology at the University of Rhode Island who was not involved in either study. This “phenotypic flexibility” in birds has been shown to vary according to seasons and population, and these studies are some of the first to demonstrate this across species and subspecies at the mitochondrial level.
“Such a theme,” he said, “is centrally important for understanding how birds during migration accomplish their athletic feats.”

data.author: jruohonen
data.article_summary: 《苏联国民车：拉达的持久遗产》文章简要总结了拉达汽车的历史和影响。20世纪60年代，苏联与意大利菲亚特公司合作，引进了先进汽车技术，打造了适应本国条件的拉达2101车型。这款车简单耐用，价格实惠，迅速成为苏联人民的国民车，象征着新的社会流动性和国家自豪感。随后推出的拉达Niva在国内外市场也大获成功，成为苏联出口的盈利产品，扩展了其国际影响力。尽管苏联解体，拉达品牌依然存在，全球销量超过2000万辆，并在俄罗斯市场占有重要地位。然而，其安全性能曾受到批评。
